articleTitle: Integrating Supervised and Probabilistic Learning: A Hybrid SVM-Naive Bayes Framework for Enhanced Emotional Insight Extraction from Twitter Streams
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Online social networks have become essential platforms for individuals to share their thoughts and opinions with friends, family, and the broader community on various topics. Through text, picture, audio, and video communications, people may communicate their ideas, feelings, and opinions on social, political, and other issues. Text is still the most popular way for people to express themselves on social networks, even with the wide range of communication types accessible. The aim of this research is to identify and examine the emotions expressed by students via their Twitter tweets. The COVID-19 pandemic has affected students in a variety of ways, resulting in a rise in social media posts highlighting these problems, lockdowns, and related hashtags, both positively and negatively. The study assesses public opinion on actions taken during such times, as well as the different emotional reactions of students to these stressors and related issues. This is accomplished by applying a combination of probabilistic learning and supervised learning using SVM and Naive Bayes classifiers for text categorization, offering a rapid and accurate approach. Predictive models are trained using the Semantic-based Feature Extraction and Feature Selection techniques. This approach allows for the detection of a wide variety of expressed emotions, making it easier to provide appropriate support when necessary.

articleTitle: LoRa WAN Based Smart System for Unsafe Event Detection in Mining Industry Using ML
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Protection of the workforce in any organization not to mention at the mining grade is a key factor that ought to be considered by any business. This is especially critical, from the health perspective of the employees and the overall health of the corporation in question. Clean fresh air is essential to the welfare of the mining workers and their overall health. A classical model of smart systems has been Lower has been established in the mining industry to introduce a LoRa based to detect hazardous events in mining zones. The developed prototype can detect the quality of air, humidity, temperature, and landslides. Air quality depends on the saturation of harmful gases such as methane gas with the aid of MQ4, MQ7 & Optical dust Sensors. The temperature and humidity of the atmosphere are measured by the DHT11 Sensor. Flame and accelerometer sensors are required for the identification of fire accidents and landsides of mining Zones. Any vehicular accident can be predicted using a machine learning model by training data obtained from various sensors in a sensor node by employing ML. In line with this, most decisions can be made using opted-ML on the devices without the need to transfer data to the actual cloud leading to better efficiency and security. Automatic notification and response to the scene with the online evacuation route assistance in case of an emergency, for instance, fires or gas leaks, can be offered by IoT. Implementation is a bit divided into two parts that include the Transmitter module and the Receiver Module with the LoRa through IoT (LoRaWAN).

articleTitle: A Comparative Evaluation of H-Infinity and PI Controllers with Emphasis on Motor Selection for BLDC Motor Speed Control in Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: In this paper, we present a comprehensive study on the selection of motors and controllers for electric vehicles (EVs), focusing on the Brushless DC (BLDC) motor. A comparative analysis is performed between H-Infinity and Proportional- Integral (PI) controllers for the purpose of speed control. According to simulation data, the H- Infinity controller works better in dynamic settings than the PI controller in terms of accuracy and resilience. The results substantiate the use of H - Infinity as the optimal choice for BLDC motor speed control in EVs.

articleTitle: Design and Modeling of Shape Memory Alloy Spring Actuated Microsystem
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: All the materials in globe have its own resistivity property in general. This resistive property is considered for its electrical conduction behaviour. Most commonly, the physical parameters like temperature, pressure, strain, and strength of a material may vary whenever a material gets electricity in it. Shape Memory Alloys also gets those parameters change while experiencing electricity. Shape Memory Alloys (SMA) are widely used in many sectors, like industrial, medical and robotics for its flexibility with electrical resistance, light weight and phase reformation behaviour in thermal environment. NiTinol is one of the Shape Memory Alloy which is frequently used for commercial applications. SMA has shape change due to the temperature change. It has three stages of shapes (cooled shape, heated shape, and natural shape) in its thermal environment. In this paper these shape change due to the electrically created thermal environment is modelled and temperature variation may analysed using COMSOL.A design of Microsystem based on SMA spring is the main focus for this research work. Mechanical behaviour is also modelled for SMA spring under electrically created thermal environment. Mainly nonlinear actuation of a SMA is concentrated.

articleTitle: An IoT-Based Power Monitoring Solution with Real-Time Data Display
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: An Arduino Uno-based real-time energy monitoring system was developed to track and display electrical power usage effectively. The system was designed using an Arduino microcontroller board, current sensors, an LCD display, and smartphone connectivity for remote monitoring. The primary objective was to provide users with instant access to energy consumption data, enabling them to manage and optimize their power usage efficiently. The current sensor measured the electrical load, and the data was processed by the microcontroller, which subsequently displayed the information on the LCD screen and transmitted it to a connected smartphone. The system's performance was tested under varying electrical loads, and consistent, accurate data collection was confirmed. The results demonstrated that real-time updates were displayed clearly, and remote monitoring was reliable, enhancing user convenience. The system's ease of use and affordability make it an accessible tool for residential and small business applications. Key advantages included user-friendly installation, stable power supply integration, and compatibility with common smart home technologies. Future enhancements could involve improving communication modules and expanding functionality for larger-scale energy management. This research highlights the potential for implementing practical, cost-effective energy solutions that contribute to smarter energy use and conservation, supporting sustainable practices and more informed decision-making for energy consumption.

articleTitle: Synergizing Support Vector Machines and Image Processing for Superior Skin Cancer Detection : A Crammer-Singer Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Skin cancer, which primarily impacts skin exposed to ultraviolet (UV) rays against the sun, represents dangerous to the most significant organs in the human body, the skin. Usually, a spot, lump, or mole that appears on the skin is the primary suspicion of skin cancer. However, each of these can undergo changes in coloring or shape as time passes. Recovery for skin cancer is mostly possible if the disease is discovered early. Numerous medical diagnostic methods, such as Dermoscopy, biopsy, and ocular examination of the affected area, are useful in helping anticipate the development of skin cancer. However, these approaches have the disadvantage of delivering erroneous results because it is extremely difficult to distinguish between normal and malignant skin. Therefore, the drawback of these diagnostic procedures is that machine learning algorithms are currently used together with image processing techniques to examine the images for the purpose of precisely identifying skin cancer. The current research employs the ISIC dataset to develop a novel model for skin cancer classification that combines image processing techniques with advanced machine learning methods, including Crammer-Singer Support vector machine learning algorithms. The categorization of skin cancer begins with preprocessing the input image, which includes hair removal using a morphological filter and image enhancement using a median filter to minimize noise and increase image clarity. The ABCD approach is used to segment lesion images by evaluating them for asymmetry, border irregularity, color variability, and diameter. The crammer-Singer SVM algorithm is then used with these images to classify skin lesions into various types such as melanoma (MEL), melanocytic nevus (NV), basal cell carcinoma (BCC), actinic keratosis (AK), benign keratosis (BKL), dermatofibroma (DF), vascular lesion (VASC), and squamous cell carcinoma (SCC), leveraging its robust multi-class handling capabilities. The system achieves the maximum accuracy of 98.2% for image classification and outperforms existing approaches for skin cancer classification.

articleTitle: Leveraging Fog Computing for Task Offloading in IoT Networks: A Focus on Deadline and Computation Demand Management
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Efficient task offloading to fog nodes (FNs) is crucial in Internet of Things (IoT)-fog systems to tackle the problems of high computing demands and stringent deadlines of IoT tasks. In order to optimize task offloading, this study proposes a model DCTO (deadline and computation demand-based task offloading) that makes use of fog computing (FC). The goals of DCTO are to minimize the overall offloading delay, energy usage. The model suggested, ensures a fair distribution of tasks across available FNs integrating efficient decision-making algorithm by controlling task's computing demand and their deadline. The proposed approach's effectiveness is compared with First-Come-First-Serve (FCFS), RANDOM algorithm, Deadline-based algorithm (DA) and confirmed by extensive simulations, which show notable improvements over traditional methods from the perspective of offloading delay, energy efficiency as well.

articleTitle: Smart Shoes for Athletes: A Sustainable Approach for Monitoring and to Improve Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Smart shoes are an exciting combination of tech and footwear that bring new ways to improve mobility and monitor health. These shoes are equipped with sensors and technology that track movement, analyze walking patterns and collect biometric data in real time. This article looks at how smart shoes are designed, what they can do, and how they can be used in sports and everyday activities. By fitting seamlessly into our daily lives, smart shoes could change how we perform in sports, helping us to be our best and stay healthy. In addition, progress in AI and data analysis plays a crucial role in enhancing and personalizing the features of smart shoes. This makes them essential tools for those looking to enhance their physical fitness, avoid injuries, and monitor chronic ailments. As the popularity of wearable tech increases, smart shoes become a versatile and indispensable resource for promoting healthier lifestyles and improved mobility. Furthermore, the utilization of piezoelectric power from walking generates energy that can be harnessed for shoes and other applications

articleTitle: A Power Efficient 45nm CMOS Dynamic Comparator with Integrated Charge Pump for Enhanced Speed Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Comparators are fundamental components in mixed-signal circuits, including data converters, memory sensing circuits, and digital I/O circuits. Their performance is crucial, especially since power consumption is often a critical constraint in these applications. Comparators significantly impact the overall power budget, particularly in battery-operated devices where efficiency is paramount. In high-speed and high-precision applications, the delay of comparators is vital for overall system performance. Managing this delay is essential for optimal functionality. A low-power, high-speed dynamic comparator has been developed, featuring a pre-amplifier, a decision circuit, and a charge pump. The charge pump enhances speed by boosting voltage, allowing for faster switching of internal transistors, which reduces response times. According to the simulation results, the comparator demonstrates a power consumption of 11.8 μW along with a rapid delay time of 30.92 ps. The design was simulated using Cadence Virtuoso in 45nm CMOS technology, operating at a clock frequency of 1 GHz and a supply voltage of 1 V. The combination of low power and high speed, facilitated by the charge pump, highlights the effectiveness of this comparator design for meeting the stringent requirements of mixed-signal applications.

articleTitle: A Novel Study on Deep Learning Based Adversarial Attack Techniques on Digit Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This research study presents a comparative analysis of four adversarial attack techniques-Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM), Basic Iterative Method (BIM), Jacobian Based Saliency Map Attack (JBSM), and Carlini & Wagner (C&W) -on MNIST dataset. Evaluation of each technique's effectiveness is based on metrics such as overall accuracy on adversarial images, mean prediction probability drop, successful attack rate, and confidence reduction. The FGSM attack achieves a moderate overall accuracy of 62.22 % and a successful attack rate of 37.78%, demonstrating moderate effectiveness. In contrast, BIM and JBSM exhibit higher effectiveness, with overall accuracies of 6.67% and 4.44%, and successful attack rates of 93.33% and 95.56%, respectively. The C& W attack is notably the most effective, reducing accuracy to 0.00% and achieving a 100% successful attack rate. Proposed work highlights the varying impact of these techniques, with C&W being the most potent in degrading model performance and suggesting the need for targeted defences against specific attack types.

articleTitle: Efficient Li-Fi based Tollgate System with Solar Power and Automation for Seamless Transactions
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The motivation behind developing a Li-Fi-based toll collection system stems from the need to modernize vehicle communication and ensure efficient and contactless information exchange between vehicle and tollgate. The problem lies in the current limitations of toll collection, which relies on outdated radio or manual signaling methods. These methods may not provide energy harvesting and timely communication during emergencies. To address these challenges, a Li-Fi-based toll collection system is proposed. This system utilized Light Fidelity (Li-Fi) technology, which uses visible light to transmit data wirelessly using Arduino Nano, ESP32 microcontroller, and a solar panel are integrated to ensure seamless, contactless communication. The Arduino Nano handles the input system, gathering data of vehicle number. This data is transmitted via a light-based communication channel to a toll collection point, where a solar panel is the receiver. The ESP32 module processes the data, ensuring secure and energy-efficient operation. Real-time feedback is provided through an LCD for easy monitoring. The results of this approach demonstrate that Li-Fi technology offers a faster, more reliable, and more secure communication system compared to traditional radio or manual methods.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Silicon Carbide Processing for Power MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Power electronics focuses on improving power density, efficiency, and the integration of systems. Key to this development are power semiconductor devices, which control electric energy efficiently from the source to the load based on the load's needs. This project examines silicon carbide (SiC) power MOSFETs, looking at various processing techniques. It studies the SiC material to see how its structure and impurities affect its performance. Using Technology Computer-Aided Design (TCAD), researchers simulate and optimize SiC devices. SiC is known for its excellent electrical, thermal, and mechanical properties, making it suitable for high- power and high-temperature applications. TCAD lets researchers study how electric charges move, how heat behaves, and how electric fields interact within SiC devices. This helps in predicting performance, spotting issues, and designing SiC devices that are more efficient and reliable. By doing this, the development of SiC technology is accelerated, which benefits areas like power electronics, telecommunications, and renewable energy systems.

articleTitle: Vehicle Detection, Counting and Classification Using YOLOv8 Deep Learning Model and OpenCV for Urban Traffic Management System
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: In this paper YOLOv8 deep learning model is proposed for vehicle detection, classification, and counting for urban traffic surveillance applications on custom dataset. The model was trained with images and annotations done using the CVAT annotation tool, and it implemented in real-time using a mobile phone camera as a webcam via USB. The model accurately detected and classified four categories of vehicles such as two wheelers, three wheelers, four wheelers and large vehicles. A unique tracking ID approach was implemented to count the vehicles accurately. The obtained results prove the potential of custom model for vehicle detection and classification. The proposed model detects two wheelers, three wheelers, four wheelers and large vehicles with an accuracy of 93.6%, 86.4%, 88% and 89% respectively.

articleTitle: Multi-Modal Medical Image Fusion Based on cGAN and the Curvelet Transform with 3D Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: A novel Multi-modal Medical Image Fusion technique combining Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (ConditionalGenerative Adversarial Networks (cGAN)) and the Curvelet Transform for 3D medical images. The Curvelet Transform decomposes input images into multi-scale and multi-directional features, capturing essential edges and textures, while the cGAN (Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks), conditioned on the modality type, intelligently fuses complementary information from different medical scans such as CT, MRI, and PET. By incorporating 3D imaging, the method enhances spatial coherence and volumetric accuracy, making it particularly effective for complex cases like brain imaging and tumor detection. Experimental results on multi-modal medical datasets demonstrate superior image quality with improved edge preservation, texture detail, and contrast, outperforming traditional fusion techniques. This method offers a powerful tool for enhancing diagnostic accuracy and supporting clinical decision-making through clearer and more comprehensive fused images.

articleTitle: Dimensional Dental Model Using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) & Faster R-CNN Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This study presents an advanced framework for analyzing Dental Panoramic Radiographs (DPRs) to enhance dental diagnostics through image processing, segmentation, and integration of deep learning models. The process begins with sophisticated image pre-processing, including segmentation and enhancement techniques such as flat field correction, morphological operations, and single-tooth extraction, to isolate individual teeth and enhance clarity. Transfer learning is applied using various Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to extract features and identify dental conditions. A Faster R-CNN architecture, supported by the most accurate CNN model, is utilized to detect and classify conditions with improved efficiency. Additionally, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks are incorporated to handle temporal dependencies in sequential data, refining segmentation and detection accuracy. Custom data augmentation and optimization of hyperparameters further enhance the performance of the models. Validation through k-fold cross-validation reveals a high diagnostic accuracy of 98%, emphasizing the potential of this approach to automate dental disease detection and assist in treatment planning.

articleTitle: Integrating Stacking Ensembles with SVM Kernels for High-Fidelity Malware Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Malicious software, or malware, is programming code that infiltrates computer systems through security holes. This research paper presents an all-inclusive study on improving the malware detection process using ensemble-based and kernel-specific machine-learning classification techniques. Advanced cyber threats require the most advanced solutions that can effectively balance accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score for robust malware identification. The proposed methodology combines the diversity of models, including SVM using its linear, polynomial, and radial basis function (RBF) kernels, and a stacking classifier that aggregates these base models to take advantage of the strengths of the individual components. The analysis concludes with stronger proof that the stacking classifier performs better, gaining the highest accuracy at 98.57% and retaining good precision and recall for all the metrics involved in the evaluation. This paper identifies a major need for hybrid and ensemble methods in cybersecurity and suggests how they can further increase detection rates while reducing false classifications. Future work can further integrate the adaptation towards incorporating more advanced ensemble strategies along with deep learning models and explainable AI (XAI) techniques aimed to optimize model transparency and performance into adaptability to provide effectiveness in sophisticated and evolving malware threats.

articleTitle: Optimizing Packet Delivery in Underwater Wireless Sensor Networks: A Comparative Study of Genetic Bee Colony and Ant Colony Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Physically Underwater communication adopt the bio inspired genetic bee colony formed network communication structures. Underwater environment condition Communication is established between the Transmitting node and in between several clustering relay nodes to reach receiver nodes. Transmitting nodes are placed on sea bed areas at certain depth and clustering relay nodes are placed in various underwater depth conditions dipping the sensor nodes. Also, underwater battery life is very hard and battery replacement is a very tough task. Hence, an alternate solution of optimization battery capacity utilization is used. This optimization algorithm improves Packet delivery ratio by comparing genetic bee algorithm with Ant colony algorithm. Hence, equivalence of two algorithms implemented in underwater conditions. The genetic bee colony Algorithm produces better output results more than 4 to 6 percentage compared to ant colony parameter output. The genetic bee colony algorithm offers a maximum clustering node technique compared to ant colony algorithm. Its greater support for saving energy consumption extending battery life.

articleTitle: A Review Investigation on Current Trends in Smart Unsighted Cane Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Blindness and other forms of vision impairment affect millions of people globally. By 2015,940 million people will have some degree of vision loss, predicts the World Health Organization. Most people with poor vision are above an age of 50 years. The advancement of technology has significantly improved the quality of life for individuals with visual impairments. Smart blind sticks, also known as electronic white canes or smart canes, are innovative devices that integrate cutting-edge technologies to enhance mobility, safety, and independence for visually impaired individuals. The review paper explores potential future approaches, including the integration of artificial intelligence and energy-efficient technology, and identifies present problems and constraints, including cost, power consumption, and social acceptance. This study seeks to contribute to the improvement of smart blind stick technologies, ultimately enhancing the quality of life for those who are visually impaired by offering a thorough analysis of recent developments.

articleTitle: Evaluating and Contrasting the Performance of Web Development Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The next generation of webpages is heavily influenced by large scale, high concurrency, and massive amounts of data. Building data-intensive web apps has made Node.js popular and effective. We employed scenario testing and benchmark testing to examine and contrast the performance of Node.js, Python-Web, and PHP. Per the testing results, PHP and Python-Web handle a lot less requests in a given amount of time than Node.js, which is evident from some useful performance metrics. Our findings, taken together, show that Node.js is the most lightweight and efficient of the three, making it a good choice for I/O-intensive websites; PHP, on the other hand, is best suited for small- to medium-sized applications, while Python-Web is developer-friendly and excels at large web architectures. This research study includes the performance evaluation of web development technologies.

articleTitle: Unveiling Network Anomalies: A Machine Learning Approach to Intrusion Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This study investigates the efficacy of different machine learning(ML) models for detecting intrusions using the LUFlow dataset, which comprises comprehensive network traffic data. An Intrusion Detection System (IDS) is an essential component of network security, intending to detect the goal of detecting unauthorised entries or abnormalities that may signal hostile actions in this environment. Four major ML models: Logistic Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), AdaBoost, and XGBoost models have been assessed all providing unique benefits in terms of interpretability, robustness, and performance. The dataset undergoes extensive preprocessing to guarantee that the data is error-free, pertinent to the task at hand, and appropriate for modelling purposes. This entails managing missing values, standardising numerical characteristics, coding variables with categories, and dividing the data into sets for training, validation, and testing. Preprocessing processes are crucial for enhancing the quality and dependability of the dataset, hence improving the accuracy and resilience of the models. By conducting a methodical assessment, the objective is to ascertain the most efficient ML algorithm for identifying intrusions in network data. The research findings have important implications for improving network security by offering a strong tool for detecting and preventing harmful activity in network environments at an early stage.

articleTitle: Empowering the Blind School Communities by Recognition of Handwritten Braille Text Documents Using YOLOv5 Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Braille is a tactile writing system that consists of raised dots arranged in a 3×2 grid for those who are visually handicapped. To empower blind school populations, this project focuses on identifying handwritten Kannada Braille text documents specifically gathered from educational institutions. The handwritten Braille has unique challenges such as variability in dot formation, differences in spacing of dots, and limited available datasets, which impact recognition accuracy and reliability. Recent findings in deep learning such as Convolution Neural Networks [CNNs] and You Only Look Once [YOLOv5]-based models have improved image recognition but struggle with irregularities in handwritten Braille texts. To address these challenges, this project aims to empower blind schools by accurately identifying the Kannada handwritten Braille texts using YOLOv5, a real-time object detection. A dataset of 1500 samples from Kaggle is used to train the model, and 1000 samples gathered from these educational institutions are used to validate it. With a 5.832% loss and an accuracy of 94.168%, the results show that YOLOv5 is a useful technique for real-world Kannada Braille character recognition.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Plant Health Monitoring: A CNN-Based Solution
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Plants are essential to country economy, agriculture, and climatic stability. However, a number of illnesses brought on by fungus, viruses, and bacteria pose a threat to plant health, thus early disease diagnosis is essential to preventing extensive damage. In this paper, a deep learning-based model for leaf image-based plant disease diagnosis is introduced. The Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) used in the suggested model was trained on the Plant Village dataset and has numerous convolution and pooling layers. The dataset is expanded by the use of data augmentation techniques, which guarantees strong model performance. After training, the model evaluated on 80% of the dataset, which contains photos of both healthy and ill plants, and it obtained a high accuracy of 86.3%. The study provides a more objective and effective method of identifying plant diseases by demonstrating the usefulness of deep learning or plant disease recognition. Future integration of the model with drones or automated systems could facilitate real-time disease detection and localization, enabling timely intervention in the agricultural field.

articleTitle: Enhancing Gaussian Mixture Model Efficiency Through Covariance Matrix Optimization, Singular Value Decomposition, and Block Toeplitz Matrices
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Gaussian Mixture Models (GMMs) are widely used for clustering, density estimation, and pattern recognition. Despite their versatility, GMMs often face computational challenges, particularly when dealing with large datasets or high-dimensional spaces. To address these issues, an approach is proposed to enhance the efficiency of GMMs by integrating covariance matrix optimization, Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), and Block Toeplitz matrices. The method involves refining the covariance matrix to better capture the underlying data structure, thereby reducing computational complexity. The application of SVD allows for dimensionality reduction and improved numerical stability. Additionally, the use of Block Toeplitz matrices facilitates efficient handling of structured covariance matrices, further accelerating computations. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in prediction accuracy and computational speed, providing a more scalable and efficient solution for GMM applications across various domains.

articleTitle: A Fertilizer Recommendation System for Rice Leaf Plant
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The secret to increasing crop productivity and sustainability is precision farming. Optimizing fertilizer use is essential in rice cultivation to satisfy the unique nutrient requirements of crops while reducing environmental effect. Conventional techniques focus on general principles, which frequently result in reduced yields, deteriorated soil, and inefficient nutrient usage. The AI-based fertilizer recommendation system RiceFert, created for rice leaf plants, is presented in this work. The system examines crop-specific information, soil characteristics (such as type and nutrient levels), and environmental data (temperature, humidity, and wetness) using a Random Forest (RF) model and deep learning techniques. Data preparation, feature extraction, and model training are all part of the process, which compares classifiers such as Random Forest, SVM, Gradient Boosting, and Naive Bayes. The Random Forest model is superior at recommending fertilizer based on performance criteria like accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. This focused strategy reduces excessive or inadequate fertilizer use, increasing rice output and promoting sustainable farming. RiceFert demonstrates the potential of AI in precision agriculture by offering farmers personalized guidance that improves crop output, lowers costs, encourages environmental conservation, and helps farmers make better decisions.

articleTitle: Analyzing Dynamic Workload Management and Energy-Efficient Task Scheduling in Cloud Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Cloud computing provides flexible and scalable solutions for diverse applications, but effective task scheduling remains a critical challenge that significantly impacts performance, resource allocation, and operational costs. This paper examines the complexities of task scheduling in dynamic cloud environments, with a particular emphasis on optimizing energy efficiency and improving workload management. Traditional heuristic-based approaches often struggle to address the challenges posed by dynamic, large-scale cloud systems. The paper reviews energy-efficient scheduling strategies for their potential to reduce energy consumption while maintaining system performance. Furthermore, it explores advanced scheduling techniques, including hybrid heuristics, machine learning-based methods, and optimization algorithms. By critically analyzing the current state of research and identifying key challenges, this study aims to propose innovative solutions to enhance resource utilization, minimize energy costs, and improve the overall efficiency of cloud task scheduling.

articleTitle: Electric Mobility through Dynamic Wireless Energy Transfer Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The rapid embracement of Electric Vehicles (EVs) is transforming the transportation field, necessitating innovative solutions for efficient energy transfer. This project explores express-way dynamic wireless energy transfer for electric vehicles as a transformative approach to charging EVs on the move. By integrating advanced resonant inductive coupling techniques and real-time vehicle localization, our technology enables continuous charging while maintaining high energy efficiency and minimal disruption to traffic flow. Through simulations and prototype testing, we demonstrate the feasibility and benefits of dynamic wireless energy transfer, highlighting its potential to enhance the user experience and support the growth of sustainable transportation infrastructure. As the adoption of EVs accelerates, traditional charging methods present challenges such as downtime and infrastructure limitations. This project highlights the feasibility of express-way dynamic wireless energy transfer as a pivotal technology in advancing sustainable transportation and addresses the technical challenges inherent in its implementation.

articleTitle: Real-Time Traffic Density Monitoring and Adaptive Signal Control Using YOLOv8 and Arduino-Based LED System
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This research paper introduces a real-time adaptive traffic management system designed to improve urban transportation efficiency and emergency vehicle prioritization. The system integrates advanced machine learning and IoT technologies, using the YOLOv8 object detection model and an Arduino-based microcontroller to monitor vehicle density, detect emergency vehicles, and dynamically manage traffic signals. The proposed solution incorporates multiple features, including software-controlled signals and real-time ambulance detection, to address the limitations of conventional fixed-timer traffic systems. Sensors and cameras capture live traffic data, which is processed to categorize density levels—Easy, Medium, and Heavy—for each direction (North, South, East, West). The integration of real-time data with dynamic signalling reduces traffic congestion while ensuring uninterrupted passage for emergency vehicles. Key innovations include an ambulance detection feature, which overrides normal traffic logic to immediately provide green-light passage, and centralized software management for greater flexibility and scalability. The YOLOv8 model, trained on a dataset of 10,000 annotated images, achieves a detection accuracy of 97.8%, ensuring precise and reliable operation. Experimental results demonstrate a 30% reduction in congestion wait times and a 40% improvement in ambulance response times. By leveraging real-time data and automated decision-making, this intelligent traffic management system addresses critical urban traffic challenges, offering a scalable and cost-effective solution. The system enhances operational efficiency and emergency response, marking a significant advancement in modern transportation networks.

articleTitle: Advanced Deep Learning Algorithm for Offline Signature Fraud Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: One of the biometric methods for personal identification that is commonly employed is signature verification. The method of verifying a signature in many business contexts, including bank check payments, relies on a human scrutiny of a single known sample. Few attempts have been undertaken to conduct the verification based on a single reference sample, despite the fact that automatic signature verification has been the subject of much research. This paper proposes an offline method for verifying handwritten signatures using deep convolutional neural networks (DNNs), an explainable deep learning technique, and a feature extraction methodology based on BRISK. The advantages of Binary Robust Invariant Scalable Key-points (BRISK) over the Fast and SURF algorithms include much simpler computations, the use of distance rather than Euclidean distance, and faster execution times. We train our system on the open source document analysis and recognition (ICDAR)2011 Sigcomp dataset which helps us determine if a questioned signature is authentic or a fake. Every sample that we utilize for testing comes from a new author whose signature are absent from the training. The testing dataset has a higher accuracy based on the experimental outcomes

articleTitle: AI-Driven Retention: A Hybrid Approach to Employee Turnover Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Predictive analytics by combining ensemble learning and deep learning techniques. The first step normalizes the feature space with MinMaxScaler, which improves the performance of the algorithms. To tackle class imbalances, the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) is used, ensuring strong predictive modeling. An empirical study shows the effectiveness of various algorithms, including ensemble methods like CatBoost, AdaBoost, LightGBM, and Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM), whicheffectively capture complex interactions and nonlinear relationships in employee data. Furthermore, Long Short- Term Memory (LSTM) networks are employed to identify temporal dependencies in longitudinal records. The findings emphasize the approach's capability to detect subtle signals of potential turnover. By integrating these methodologies, this research provides HR professionals with valuable tools for proactive retention strategies. Ultimately, it advances HR analytics, assisting organizations in reducing attrition risks and promoting an engaged workforce.

articleTitle: Hyper parameter-Tuned SGD and GB Techniques for Enhanced Accuracy in Mental Health Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This study applies Improved machine learning methods for predicting the mental health treatment, thus, making classification accuracy stronger which will correspondingly lead to better early intervention. With the help of Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) and Gradient Boosting, the study entrains the treatment status by utilization of the patient attributes. Data preprocessing included the missing value treatment, categorization conversion, and standardization of numerical variables, and therefore improved data modeling. Hyper parameter tuning via GridSearchCV process was able to find the optimal parameters for the two models, and the highest accuracy in terms of mental health data is crucial to analyze, with correct estimations of precision and recall across all classes. For Tuned Gradient Boosting classifier Area Under Curve (AUC) is 0.86. Key performance metrics including F1-score and AUC reflected the superior capability of Gradient Boosting to discover complex patterns in the dataset. These results will lead to real-time mental health evaluation and proper management for individuals.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Accuracy of Human Activity Recognition Using Smartphones Using a Hybrid LR-NN Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: In present days Human Activity Recognition (HAR) using smart phones getting more attention as its crucial for applications like fitness tracking conditions, health monitoring systems, and adaptive services. The goal of this work is to increase the accuracy and reliability of HAR systems using a hybrid technique that combines Logistic Regression (LR) and Neural Networks (NN). Through the attainment and combination of sensor data from smartphones, for example accelerometer and gyroscope interpretations, the hybrid model achieves both the complex pattern recognition power of Neural Networks and the flexibility and easy readability of Logistic Regression. The model initially works to learns the linear relationships using LR and then it trains using NN to enhance the classification metrics. With this hybrid technique the capability of decision making is improved by combining the probabilistic outputs. The results concluded that the accuracy is enhanced to 98% in classifying the exact outcome.

articleTitle: Secure and Fault-Tolerant Block Memory Design for IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This study introduces a secure and fault-tolerant block memory design tailored for Internet of Things (IoT) applications. The architecture integrates advanced encryption methods, dual-port memory access, and parity-based error detection to enhance data security and precision. Additionally, dynamic power management strategies minimize energy consumption, making the design highly suitable for IoT's resource-constrained environments. The IoT role is further emphasized through real- time data processing and remote accessibility features, addressing key security challenges in cloud-based applications. The design, implemented in Verilog and validated on the Vivado platform, shows measurable improvements in reliability, error resilience, and power efficiency, offering a robust solution for secure memory storage in IoT systems.

articleTitle: Empirical Evaluation of Activation Functions and Solvers on Neural Network Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This study evaluates the impact of activation functions and solvers on neural network performance using the Or ange data analytics platform. Twelve combinations of four activation functions (Identity, Logistic, Tanh, ReLU) and three solvers (L-BFGS-B, SGD, Adam) were tested with 100 hidden neurons, a 0.0001 regularization parameter, and 200 iterations. ReLU combined with L-BFGS-B, SGD, and Adam solvers achieved the highest accuracy (98<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) and MCC (0.973), highlighting optimal configurations for enhanced neural network performance.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence and Chatbots: Transforming User Experience in E-tailing
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and chatbots have become essential components of the e-commerce industry, providing significant advantages for both businesses and consumers. AI utilizes data to tailor customer interactions, forecast their needs, and refine decision-making processes, resulting in a smoother and more enjoyable shopping experience. AI-driven chatbots, in particular, are instrumental in offering immediate assistance, addressing customer queries, and providing 24/7 support. This study aims to investigate the impact of AI and Amazon's chatbot technology on customer satisfaction among Amazon users in Bengaluru. A quantitative research approach was employed, gathering data from 150 active Amazon customers through online surveys. Regression analysis reveals that AI-enhanced features and chatbot services notably improve customer satisfaction (p < 0.001). Factors such as the chatbot's ease of use, fast response times, and accurate information contribute significantly to this positive effect. These findings highlight the critical role of AI-powered customer service solutions in e-commerce, emphasizing their potential to enhance user experiences and build long-term customer loyalty.

articleTitle: A 60-90 GHz 90-nm CMOS Low Noise Amplifier with Optimum NF for Radio Astronomy Receivers
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The detection of radio signals from distant astronomical sources is crucial to the field of radio astronomy, as it enhances our understanding of the universe. To optimize noise reduction during the amplification process, Low Noise Amplifiers (LNA) play a vital role in amplifying these weak signals. The LNA topology includes a common gate for input impedance matching, a common drain for output impedance matching, and an active feedback network configuration designed to minimize noise. This LNA operates across the entire E-band frequency range of 60–90 GHz and is implemented using 90nm CMOS technology. It achieves an average noise figure of 1 dB, with a minimum noise figure of 0.14 dB. Additionally, it consumes 11mW of DC power and delivers a peak power gain of 40 dB. Ultimately, this advanced approach enables radio astronomers to discover new celestial phenomena by facilitating more effective communication networks.

articleTitle: Secure Data Flow Between Trusted Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Nowadays, traditional networks like organizational networks or home networks are widely used, but networks can be vulnerable to security threats, especially from insider attacks. These networks focus more on encryption, authentication, and access control, and they neglect the crucial parts like node behaviour. This is where the concept of trusted networks comes into existence. A trusted network is a group of devices that are known to be safe and secure for communication, not only based on authentication but also based on their behaviour. This paper introduces a novel approach to building secure data flow between trusted networks by analyzing node behaviour. The main idea is to build trust based on four main parameters similarity, direct trust, risk assessment, and reputation. Along with the traditional security measures, this approach continuously monitors and adjusts trust levels based on the observed behaviour of nodes. By isolating nodes or giving a high trust level that exhibits malicious or risky behaviour, the trusted network remains secure for data flow. The proposed method is implemented and evaluated through simulations, demonstrating its effectiveness in establishing trusted networks and enabling secure communication.

articleTitle: Velocity Control of DC Motor Using Smart Voice Announcement System
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This research introduces an innovative method for regulating the velocity of a DC motor through intelligent voice recognition technology. By utilizing the advancements in voice recognition algorithms, a hardware system has been developed to interpret the voice commands accurately for adjusting the speed of the DC motor. This system comprises of a microphone for voice input, a microcontroller for signal processing, and a motor driver for speed control. The design and implementation of the proposed system is executed through the voice recognition algorithm and a hardware setup. Furthermore, experimental validations are conducted to evaluate the systems performance and accuracy in controlling the motor speed under different conditions. The results confirm the feasibility and efficiency of the proposed method, showcasing precise and prompt speed adjustments through voice commands. Lastly, potential applications of this technology in smart home automation, robotics, and industrial control systems are discussed, highlighting the adaptability and significant impact of voice-controlled motor systems across various sectors.

articleTitle: Image Classification of House Interiors and Street Views Using Vision Transformer (ViT-B/16)
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The application of the Vision Transformer (ViT-B/I6) model for street and dwelling image classification is investigated in this work. With all photos reduced to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$224\times 224$</tex> pixels, the dataset consists in house interiors (e.g., bathrooms, kitchens) and street views (e.g., apartments, churches, industrial buildings). Leveraging self-attention strategies, the ViT model was refined to identify complex visual patterns and long-range dependencies inside the images. Using criteria including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, the model's performance was evaluated and classified accuracy of 96.75% emerged. With little misclassification, the confusion matrix and classification report showed that the model reasonably separated between house interiors and street views. Usually depending on local feature detection, the ViT-B/I6's global attention strategy helped it to surpass conventional convolutional neural networks (CNNs). This work emphasizes the possibilities of transformer-based models such as ViT for image classification tasks including various and challenging images. ViT models provide better accuracy and generalization in real-world uses including real estate analysis or urban planning by concentrating on worldwide image attributes. The results create paths for next investigation on computer vision transformer architectures.

Author Keywords: Climate Action and AI for Urban Management, etc.

articleTitle: Global Energy Consumption Patterns and Optimization using Big Data
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Energy optimization is critical for improving sustainability and energy efficiency in the face of rising global energy demand. Using big data analytics methods, this study investigates ways to optimize energy use patterns. Energy efficiency research and development are of critical importance in light of the increasing need for renewable power sources. Making reliable predictions about future energy consumption trends from existing data is the main focus of this research. The dataset contains factors like home electricity consumption, weather, and occupancy patterns; to analyze it, we used Apache Spark and Hadoop for data processing and a Random Forest regression model. The results show that the prediction accuracy is significantly higher than with standard models; the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{R}^{2}$</tex> score is more than 0.85. Also, the model finds the main things that make energy use what it is, so you may optimize your usage right now. In order to help customers and lawmakers make better judgments about energy efficiency, this study adds to the body of knowledge in energy management by offering a scalable method for predicting future energy needs. Improving predictive capacities will be the primary goal of future research, which will investigate sophisticated machine learning algorithms and integrate real-time data sources.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approach to Predict Autism Spectrum Disorder
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: These days, autism spectrum disorder, or ASD, is becoming more widespread. The process of using screening tests to find autism signs is time- and money-consuming. Because of advancements in AI and machine learning algorithms, it is now feasible to identify early indicators of autism spectrum disorder in youngsters. Additionally, a number of studies employing various methodologies have been conducted, although clear-cut conclusions about age-specific forecasting for autistic traits are lacking. Therefore, the goal of this endeavor is to create a machine-learning-based predictive model and an accessible website for the diagnosis of ASD. This study's recommended prediction model, an artificial neural network (ANN), is utilized to build a website. The model can be accessed using the AQ-10 dataset. The results of the assessments show that the prediction models outperform the datasets in terms of false positive ratio, accuracy, selectivity, responsiveness, and precision.

articleTitle: Digital Simulation of ZnON-TFT
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Modern screens largely employ the services of Thin Film Transistor (TFT) technology for improving image quality as well as making a lot of applications possible. In this work, we used Cadence Virtuoso and Verilog-A modeling to simulate and evaluate the performance of ZnON TFTs, i.e., Zinc Oxy Nitride Thin Film Transistors in a variety of circuit designs. A ZnON TFT model was designed based on the drain-to-source current equation, and its functionalities was verified in circuits like oscillator, inverters, and NAND gates were checked and compared with the experimental results to be verified. The outcome shows the correctness of the model and demonstrates how it can be applied to drive circuits and complex display technology, thereby highlighting the importance of simulation in design optimization and cost-effective development..

articleTitle: A Hybrid Cognitive-Machine Learning Approach for Personalized and Efficient Rehabilitation
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Traditional rehabilitation methods often exhibit limitations due to their focus on single impairments and lack of personalized treatment approaches. This research proposes a novel hybrid approach that integrates cognitive and machine learning models to address these limitations. The system combines meta-cognitive methodologies with dynamic adaptive training and a modified Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) using an ensemble strategy. This integrated approach enables personalized rehabilitation by tailoring treatment plans to individual patient needs and addressing multiple impairments simultaneously. The hybrid system aims to improve the effectiveness and efficiency of rehabilitation by providing personalized and adaptive interventions, ultimately leading to better patient outcomes. The proposed system aims to achieve better accuracy and efficiency compared to traditional methods. This system addresses factors such as the availability of patient data as open source, minimizes the complexity of the rehabilitation task, effective management of computational resources. Additionally, stacking, an ensemble method, mitigates individual model biases and uncertainties, enhancing the framework's reliability and adaptability to diverse patient needs and preferences. This innovative integration is expected to lead to improved patient outcomes and has the potential to be widely applicable in various rehabilitation settings.

articleTitle: Optimizing Defect Detection in Elastic Optical Networks using a Deep Neural Network and Fuzzy Logic
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The most physically pleasing structure of the remaining generation of optical fiber networks is the elastic optical network. EON seeks assurance that its infrastructure can satisfy thorough Service Level Agreements even in an environment of substantial bit-rate traffic. To attempt to solve the Routing and Spectrum Responsibilities issue with Shared Backup Path Protection, this research presents a Deep Neural Network model with a multi-objective fuzzy inference system. The method aims to enhance the trade-off between fault maintenance ratio and blockage probability. Using an original spectrum-fragmentation method increases the FRR of affected connections. Other capabilities provided through the FIS include load balancing and allocation path solution alignment.

articleTitle: Hand Gesture Implementation for Movement Automation and Health Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This research explores the advancements in smart wearables, specifically focusing on smart gloves. Equipped with advanced sensors, these gloves enable precise capture and analysis of hand and finger movements. Applications of smart gloves span various domains, including healthcare, where they can aid in the early detection and rehabilitation of motor function disorders, and enhance virtual reality experiences, training programs, and industrial operations that require precise hand movements. This technology has the potential to revolutionize various aspects of human-computer interaction and improve overall quality of life.

articleTitle: Computer-Aided Diagnosis of Intervertebral Disc Herniation from Lumbar MRI
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The approach proposed in this paper for classifying lumbar disc herniation using sagittal view magnetic resonance images (MRIs) is based on machine learning. The significant burden placed on radiologists is reduced by the automation of herniated disc diagnosis, which also helps to minimize inter- and intra-rater variability. The dataset used for this study includes 375 MRI images from 75 patients - of whom 22 are healthy, and 53 have herniated discs. To suppress undesired distortion and enhance image features to improve image quality for further operation, the MRI image is preprocessed using various Data augmentation techniques. The method consists of 4 steps mainly: Segmentation, ROI detection, Feature extraction, and Classification. Pixel intensity is considered for automatic ROI detection, and each intervertebral disc's shape, height, and width are measured. We use Support Vector Machine (SVM), Gaussian Naïve Bayes (GNB), and Logistic Regression (LR) techniques for classification and achieve an accuracy of 98.36% with Logistic Regression, 95.08% with SVM, 63.93% with Gaussian Naïve Bayes.

articleTitle: Applying Fuzzy Logic to Improve Customer Review Classification using Bidirectional LSTM Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This research study proposes a novel technique to enhance the precision of client survey segmentation. The proposed solution's offer a new understanding of linguistic uncertainty in the review text through the use of fuzzy mathematics and a bilateral Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) topology. By means of comprehensive testing, we are verifying the effectiveness of our approach in precisely classifying client input. The proposed model is outperforming traditional methods by combining fuzzy logic with bidirectional LSTM, demonstrating notable improvements in sentiment analysis. In addition to advancing the field of sentiment analysis techniques, this study offers insightful information to companies looking to better understand client sentiments.

articleTitle: AI Based Identification of Plant Health Issues
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The plant diseases detection and classification are Critical in ensuring sustainable agricultural productivity and preventing substantial crop losses. Traditional methods are time consuming and error prone and requires expertise in the field and it is difficult for larger operations. The detection of diseases using models like ResNet, MobileNet and YOLO are the recent advancements in the Artificial Intelligence and Deep Learning, but it also faces Challenges such as dataset imbalances, computational demand and variability in conditions persists. This research is on a deep learning model called Efficientnet to automate plant health diagnostics. The study evaluates the model's performance detecting various plant diseases and comparing it to other deep learning techniques, the results of the study show how Efficientnet can outperform other traditional models by providing accurate, real time plant disease identification.

articleTitle: Analysis of Performance of YOLOv8 Algorithm for Pedestrian Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Pedestrian detection is widely used nowadays in several applications like Robotics, Security systems and autonomous driving systems. Pedestrian detection is a rapidly advancing field within computer vision. Many algorithms have been developed for pedestrian detection using various deep learning approaches. Despite this development, the task of pedestrian detection from a mixed object dataset containing pedestrian and non-pedestrian images still poses a big challenge. After going through latest papers, it has been found that there is a need for enhancement in the correctness and speed of pedestrian detection for use in real world scenarios like autonomous driving systems. This paper proposes to analyze the execution of the Yolo V8algorithm with an aim of pedestrian detection. To achieve this objective, we have used machine learning pipeline from data collection to evaluation with the help of Yolo V8. The objectives of this paper are to observe and analyse the performance of the Yolo V8 model for pedestrian detection, to compare the time required by the model for two different datasets and to fine tune the model as per requirement. The Yolo v8 algorithm has demonstrated great success in the domain of computer vision for real time object detection. Initially, this algorithm was applied on the Roboflow Pedestrian Yolo V5 dataset and has shown to effectively improve pedestrian detection accuracy as the number of epochs increases. Later the algorithm was applied on the Yolo dataset Sindhi Label containing pedestrian as well as non-pedestrian images. This was done to avoid the chances of overfitting the model.

articleTitle: An Iterative PRISMA Review of Deep Learning, Sparse Bayesian, and Compressed Sensing Methods for Channel Estimation in Modern Wireless Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Accurate channel estimation is basic to efficient functioning of modern wireless communication systems, particularly in the case of 5G, mmWave, MIMO, and vehicular networks. However, most conventional techniques are usually affected by the complexity of such methods, pilot overhead, and limitations in high mobility or dynamic environments. On the other hand, in spite of a large number of proposed methods, there is a gap in covering a comprehensive and systematic survey to compare several techniques under various performance metrics. Most of the existing review articles focus on very limited sets of models and do not critically compare or contrast models based on their efficiency, accuracy, and computational complexity. To fill these gaps, this paper bases its review on state-of-the-art channel estimation models PRISMA, and included methods span traditional signal processing approaches such as LMMSE, adaptive frequency-domain estimators, and compressed sensing-based techniques, and prominent approaches based on deep learning frameworks including CNN and hybrid estimators. With the PRISMA methodology, this review provides a comprehensive analysis of the methods involved in various applications, such as MIMO, mmWave, RIS-aided systems, and underwater communications. The proposed review, on giving a number of models, discusses the pros and cons of those models. Models based on deep learning bring in an improved accuracy along with the potential of improved computational performance in estimation, whereas sparse and hybrid models have shown impressive performances in heavily resource-constrained environments such as underwater acoustic and high-mobility vehicular communications. This work will prove to be very informative for the researcher and engineer, both in showing optimal models for various applications of communication and in laying down the basis for future integration of GAN and advanced machine-learning methods into channel estimation. The outcomes derived from this review will shape and inform the future design and deployment of wireless systems through the development of a strong platform for harnessing optimization strategies in diverse applications of channel estimation.

Author Keywords: Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses Review

articleTitle: Quantum Machine Learning for the Future Medical Analysis: A Comprehensive Review and Future Prospects
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The combination of Quantum Computing with Machine Learning approaches is refered as Quantum Machine Learning (QML). Recently, there have been significant advancements in performance and computational speed to quantum computing techniques. Although traditional algorithms have shown promising outcomes, their low processing efficiency and limited labelled data are common problems. To address these issues, a great deal of research has brought machine learning and quantum computing together, which has led to the development of increasingly complex algorithms. Notable gains in parameter optimisation, execution efficiency, and error rate reduction have resulted from these developments. The incorporation of quantum machine learning has yielded novel perspectives into the transdisciplinary domain of quantum technology and medical image analysis, indicating noteworthy advancements to be made in this area going forward. QML is becoming known for its unique superposition and entanglement capabilities, which make it a cutting-edge approach to challenges involving categorization. Its uses in fields such as pattern identification, password cracking, and medical image analysis have attracted a lot of attention. Because of this, a growing number of academics are using QML-based algorithms to analyse medical data. This research review's key goal is to present an in-depth analysis of how QML techniques are used and involved in the medical field. This article includes a synopsis of the description and classification of quantum machine learning in addition to a rundown of the many QML techniques and how they have been used in medical image investigation during the previous years.

articleTitle: Classification of Common Insects Using Transfer Learning and ResNet50
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The escalation of the global temperature and the pressure on the fields is at an all-time high. To feed the rising population, insecticides, and pesticides are likewise at an all-time high. With the growing temperature due to global warming and the increasing employment of pesticides to feed the people, one class of creatures suffers the direct hit: insects. On the other hand, the growing warmth leaves them vulnerable to death due to bad environmental circumstances. On the other hand, the increasing employment of pesticides extirpates innocuous insects with hazardous insects. There is a continual requirement to monitor the growth and condition of such insects to maintain the sustainability of the environmental system. However, accomplishing such a big work manually is not only impossible but fruitless, too, since few insects of various classes provide identical looks. To cope with such challenges related to this work, a transfer learning-based ResNet50 network is presented to automatically detect, categorize, and consequently track the insect populations to take future measures. The model obtains a recognition accuracy of 91.45%.

articleTitle: Design of Mid Drive Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor for Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This research study involves the design of a permanent magnet synchronous motor, especially for mid-drive electric vehicles with medium duty. By means of using the Ansys Simulation Tool, their respective graph outputs, such as torque-speed curves, current curves, and flux distributions, are obtained, and the performance is analysed. Having the improvement on the torque handling capability. Thus, providing a possible way for real-time deployment and also being able to verify the results with the simulation output. (Abbreviations - BLDC -Brushless Dc Motor, PMSM- Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor, EV - Electric Vehicles, R&D - Research and Development, IC- Internal Combustion, AM-Amorphous metal, SS- Silicon Steel, FEM- Finite Element Method)

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Detection of Cardiovascular Diseases Using ECG Images
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: In today's world, cardiovascular disease is still a major concern. The electrocardiogram (ECG) is one of the most trustworthy non-invasive tools for identifying heart problems. ECG interpretation, however, takes a lot of effort and specialized knowledge. The quality and effectiveness of medical care are enhanced by the development of a revolutionary technique for early disease detection. Using a public dataset of ECG scans from cardiac patients, this study leveraged deep learning algorithms to predict two primary cardiac abnormalities: abnormal heartbeat and normal person classes. The low-scale pre-trained deep neural Alex Net was used to study the transfer learning process. To forecast cardiac issues, a novel Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture was put out. We used the conventional deep learning methods, VGG-16, Resnet50, RNN, and LSTM, to feature-extracted data utilizing the previously mentioned pre-trained models and our suggested LSTM model. The experimental results show that the LSTM model outperforms the previous attempts in terms of performance measures.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Multiplier in Ternary Logic Using Memristor
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Ternary systems are becoming more popular than binary systems in research areas. According to reports, ternary computing has the most potential to displace binary computers. Various types of circuits are designed in ternary systems by using various device models such as MOSFETs, CNTFETs, and memristors. Digital signal processing systems' reliability and effectiveness are impacted by multipliers' effectiveness. As a result, quick, precise ternary multipliers that can process a variety of data formats as well as signals are required. In this project, to increase the effectiveness of the multiplier design, the hybrid models which consists of both CMOS and memristor technologies used in the multiplier design. By using the memristor technology, low power consumption and less area size can be achieved. The 2 × 2 multiplier is implemented in the ternary logic system using memristor technology in the Falstad simulator and compared it with the conventional binary multiplier using CMOS technology and analyzed both multipliers in terms of power consumption and high information density.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of 3D Printed Antenna's for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This paper incorporates the design, fabrication, and evaluation of 3D-printed antennas for sub 6GHz frequencies, with a focus on patch and wideband E-shaped antennas. The wideband E-shaped antenna operates between 6.1 and 7.1 GHz, offering a bandwidth of 1–2 GHz. The design incorporates a polylactic acid (PLA) dielectric substrate positioned between a metallized ground plane and a radiating patch. Key challenges addressed include achieving dual-band operation within the 6–7 GHz range, as well as enhancing gain and bandwidth. The antennas are tested in an anechoic chamber, with performance evaluated using a Vector Network Analyzer (VNA). The dual-band antenna is then integrated with a National Instruments Universal Software Radio Peripheral (NI USRP) for real-time QPSK signal transmission and reception, demonstrating its suitability for 5G applications.

Author Keywords: Vector Network Analyzer and Universal Software Radio Peripheral

articleTitle: Smart Environmental Surveillance System for Satellite Operations
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This research focuses on developing an advanced autonomous environmental monitoring system specifically designed for satellite operations. The system uses modern sensors to collect real-time data on key environmental factors such as temperature, radiation, and atmospheric conditions that can impact satellite performance. This data is processed and displayed through an interactive, web-based dashboard, providing satellite operators with an intuitive platform for monitoring space conditions. The dashboard allows operators to visualize real-time data, detect anomalies, and track environmental trends, empowering them to make informed decisions that optimize satellite performance and ensure operational safety. The system's design emphasizes reliability and accuracy, with each sensor carefully calibrated to ensure precise data collection in the challenging and unpredictable conditions of space. By continuously tracking critical environmental variables, the system enhances situational awareness and supports more efficient management of satellite operations, enabling operators to respond proactively to changing conditions. This work directly addresses the complex challenges that satellites face in space, such as extreme temperature fluctuations and radiation exposure, contributing to the resilience and operational longevity of satellite missions. Ultimately, It aims to support the sustainable and efficient use of space resources by providing an intelligent, responsive monitoring solution for satellite operations.

articleTitle: Application of Machine Learning Algorithms for Efficient Disease Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This research presents the development of a System for Predicting Diseases Using Machine Learning. The system leverages machine learning algorithms to predict the likelihood of individuals developing COVID-19., heart disease, or chronic kidney disease. By inputting relevant symptoms, medical history, and other relevant factors, users can receive preliminary disease predictions without requiring immediate in-person consultation. Powered by Python and Django, the system provides a user-friendly interface for accessing these predictive models. This system aims to improve access to healthcare by facilitating early identification of potential health risks, empowering individuals to make informed decisions about their health, and potentially reducing the burden on healthcare systems.

articleTitle: Smart Aquarium Monitoring System for Optimal Aquatic Life Management Using IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This research proposes a novel smart automatic fish tank and fish food finder which is controlled remotely through IoT technology and is able to send email alerts. The system does away with the interference of a person on a regular basis for cleaning the aquarium by means of the servo motor revolving on a movable base plate present at the bottom of the tank. This allows for the manipulation of the amount of water that flows in and out of certain areas depending on how the base plate is tilted. This movement is what adjusts the flow of water and eventually improves the conditions of the aquarium for the creatures living inside it. It employs an IoT feature using an ESP32 to send email alerts via IFTTT when some incidents occur, e.g. low water level or high temperature.
