The purpose of this study is through the integration of its components, greatly reduce the amount of work and mistakes made during the process of taking care of the aquarium allowing time and peace of mind to aquatic fans with prompt notification system.

articleTitle: Comparative Optimization of Silicon Dioxide and Hafnium Dioxide-Based BIOFETs: Temperature Effects on Voltage and Drain Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This study examines the performance optimization of Silicon Dioxide (SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>)-based and Hafnium Dioxide (HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>)-based Biosensor Field Effect Transistors (BIOFETs) by analysing their voltage and drain current characteristics under varying temperature conditions. Experimental investigations involved two sets of BIOFET samples, each incorporating either SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> or HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> as the dielectric material. The sample size was determined with a significance level of 0.05 and a statistical power of 80%. Simulations were conducted by systematically varying the temperature from 25°C to 75°C in 5°C increments, while maintaining parameters, such as gate oxide thickness, substrate thickness, and channel length, constant. The results demonstrated significant differences in voltage and drain current characteristics between the two materials. SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-based BIOFETs exhibited higher drain current values and more stable voltage performance across the tested temperature range compared to HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-based BIOFETs. Statistical analysis using Independent T-tests confirmed these differences as significant (p < 0.05). This study highlights that SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-based BIOFETs offer superior performance over HfO2-based BIOFETs under optimized temperature conditions. These findings provide valuable insights for enhancing biosensor performance through the careful selection of dielectric materials and temperature optimization.

articleTitle: Fault Detection Algorithms for Improving Accuracy in Solar PV System
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Machine learning algorithms for fault detection in PV panels provides a powerful, scalable, and efficient solution for enhancing system reliability, reducing maintenance costs, and ensuring optimal energy production. The capacity of Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) to grasp intricate patterns and relationships from data makes them advantageous for detecting faults in photovoltaic (PV) panels. ANNs provide several advantages for fault detection in PV panels, including high accuracy, real-time monitoring, adaptability, scalability, and robustness in handling complex and noisy data. LightGBM (Light Gradient Boosting Machine) is an efficient and powerful machine learning algorithm, particularly well-suited for fault detection in photovoltaic (PV) panels. Light GBM offers several advantages, including high efficiency, scalability, and accuracy. Its ability to handle large, complex datasets with low memory consumption and computational cost makes it an excellent choice for both small and large PV systems. In this study, a comparison of these two algorithms revealed that LightGBM outperformed ANN, achieving an accuracy of 86%, compared to ANN's 74% accuracy.

articleTitle: Redefining Bone Marrow Diagnostics With AI-Driven EfficientNetB5 Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Classifying bone marrow images into different categories is challenging because there are problems like uneven class distribution, large differences within the same class, and the need for clear and accurate diagnostic models. These challenges make it hard to create reliable automated systems for clinical diagnosis. To find different blood diseases, it's important to correctly identify images of bone marrow. There are several challenges in multi-class classification, like needing clear and correct results, a lot of difference in shape among the classes, and imbalanced classes. This work looks at using a modern convolutional neural network called EfficientNetB5 to help classify bone marrow images. Our method gets 96% accuracy by using special loss functions, new ways to improve data, and easy-to-understand tools. The results show that EfficientNetB5 can make diagnoses more reliable and accurate in medical settings. We used special loss functions to fix class imbalance, advanced data enhancement methods to make our dataset more varied, and explainable techniques to ensure our model's predictions are clear and reliable, in order to address these challenges. By using EfficientNetB5's strong design, our approach gets an impressive 96% accuracy in classification, which is a big improvement.

articleTitle: Creating User Profiles Through Sentiment Analysis of Social Media
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: As social media platforms continue to expand, understanding user behavior and emotions has become essential. This paper introduces a framework for creating detailed user profiles by analyzing the sentiments expressed in their social media posts. The main aim is to identify emotional patterns in user behavior by applying sentiment analysis to social media posts and combining these insights with user engagement, thereby creating user profiles based on the preferences indicated by analyzing the different sentiments of the posts and profiles of existing users. By this means, a profile can be created that is suitable for the particular user. In this work, there are different algorithms used for sentiment analysis, and among all the algorithms, the Passive Aggressive Classifier showed a high accuracy of 72.79%. The BERT model is used for creating the profile. The dataset used in this work consists of a wide variety of data, including texts, posts, and sentiments from different social media platforms. This work mainly focuses on understanding user behavior and providing useful insights for targeted marketing and personalized content strategies, thereby enhancing user interaction on social media.

articleTitle: Solar Inverter System with 3-Phase Grid Connectivity and Supercapacitor for Enhanced Energy Efficiency and Sustainability
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: A 3-phase grid-connected hybrid solar inverter system with supercapacitor and battery backup resolves challenges of the contemporary world of the energy sector as it has high reliability, efficiency & sustainability factors. The combination of variability control and grid emulation capabilities allows the system to constantly control the power deviations thus ensuring more effective distribution of electricity. Supercapacitors are useful in providing quick responses to variability during power fluctuations. Such integration optimizes the use of solar energy which is influenced by natural variations in sunshine and fluctuates in power supply. More importantly, the system decreases the use of fossil fuels hence minimising emissions of greenhouse gases that are responsible for global warming. The dual storage approach enhances the system throughput and aligns customers, sustainable, and scalable energy storage solutions for mass deployment. This new energy management system is at once an environmental upgrade and a cost-saving innovation that holds high promise for the future of sustainable energy systems.

articleTitle: EnCR_XGBoost: Ensemble Convolutional Recurrent Based XGBoost for Autism Detection Using MRI
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The Autism detection is crucial for enhancing the social behavior and interaction of the people because the autism is a complex neurodevelopmental disorder. The deep learning based autism detection is employed for obtaining the accurate detection of disease. Still, inaccurate detection, computation complexity and over-fitting issues limit the performance. Thus, deep learning based autism detection is introduced in this research for solving the issues faced by the existing models. The input obtained from the MRI image is pre-processed using the median filter to enhance the quality of the image. Then, the appropriate features are extracted using proposed Ensemble Convolutional Recurrent (EnCR) model designed with the ensemble of convolutional and recurrent model for extracting both spatial and temporal features for enhancing the detection accuracy. Finally, XGBoost method is utilized for performing the autism detection task using the EnCR based features. The designed EnCR+XGBoost model is evaluated based on Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F-score and obtained the values of 98.1500,98.4320,98.0320, and 98.2316 respectively.

articleTitle: IoT Assisted Knee Kinematics Control for Supervised Rehabilitation of Paralyzed Patients
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This research focuses on the development of an automated knee brace for the rehabilitation of patients with paralyzed legs. The proposed system aims to replace the need for constant physiotherapist assistance by providing personalized and automated exercise routines. The system utilizes a combination of actuators, sensors, and IoT technology to control knee movements with precise speed and angle. By automating the rehabilitation process, this system aims to improve patient outcomes, accelerate recovery, and enhance the overall quality of life for individuals with paralysis. The system incorporates an 10T-based monitoring system that provides real-time data on exercise progress and alerts users to any potential issues. This research contributes to the development of innovative rehabilitation technologies that can improve patient care and enhance the independence of individuals with disabilities.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of Radar System for Detecting Stationary and Moving Targets
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Radio Detection and Ranging (RADAR) is a significant technology used for the object detection and tracking. There is regular need of advancements of the Radar as the usage is board for various applications, including weather monitoring, air traffic control, and military surveillance. This paper focuses on the enhancing the RADAR system performance by implementing the processing techniques such as (CFAR) constant false alarm rate, match filtering and Moving target indication (MTI). The CFAR algorithm helps in dynamically adjusting the threshold, can be help to avoid the false alarm rates in the cluttered environment, MTI helps to identify the moving targets and matched filtering improves the Signal to noise ratio by isolating the target signal which leads to enhancing the target accuracy. Our study shows that, even in difficult circumstances, combining these methods greatly increases the accuracy and dependability of RADAR systems. The outcomes demonstrate the higher performance that this comprehensive approach allows in a variety of operational situations, demonstrating the constant development of RADAR and its essential nature in crucial applications.

articleTitle: Nature Meets Technology: Revolutionizing Butterfly Classification with MobileNetV2
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Belonging to the order Lepidoptera, butterflies are essential ecological indicators and pollinators; nonetheless, their hand identification is difficult because of minute wing pattern differences. This work aims to build an automated butterfly classification system with MobileNetV2, a lightweight convolutional neural network architecture fit for mobile devices. Achieved via depthwise separable convolutions and an inverted residual structure, MobileNetV2's efficiency qualifies it for real-time field conditions categorization. Originating from Kaggle, the input dataset comprises 9,285 training photos and 375 images apiece for validation and testing, therefore covering 75 butterfly species. Techniques of pre-processing and augmentation were used to enhance model training so guaranteeing the diversity and quality of the dataset. The approach consisted in optimizing MobileNetV2 to fit butterfly-specific characteristics and then model evaluation depending on accuracy and other performance criteria. The results show a great classification accuracy of 94.6%, therefore verifying MobileNetV2's ability to precisely identify between species. This success emphasizes how well deep learning might monitor and protect biodiversity. The light weight architecture makes it possible to install on mobile devices, therefore enabling field real-time species identification. Future studies could increase the dataset and investigate different designs to improve the performance and applicability of the model in ecological investigations.

articleTitle: AI for Smart Agriculture – A Deep Learning Based Turmeric Leaf Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Plants is one of the major food sources for world population. In addition to that, some plants and their outcomes are used in food preparation. One of the plants which is widely used in foods and having huge medicinal value is turmeric. Curcuma long the botanically named spice turmeric has large anti-inflammatory properties, antioxidants, etc., the tropical perennial plant is cultivated worldwide. Diseases in plant leaves is one of the serious factors that affects the turmeric cultivation. Leaf disease reduces the production and it requires continuous monitoring to avoid total loss. Manual monitoring is challenging when the crop is planted in large fields. Due to industrial revolution and smart agriculture concepts, artificial intelligence- based disease detection procedure is presented in recent times. Thus, in this research work a deep learning-based turmeric leaf disease detection model is presented using AlexNet. The leaf disease classification model is experimented with our own dataset which includes diseases like Leaf Spot Disease, Leaf Blight, Leaf Rot, and Leaf Curl. The experimentation results provide the maximum accuracy of proposed leaf disease classification model as 95.5% which is better than traditional machine learning models.

articleTitle: Hand Gesture Classification for the Deaf and Mute Using the DenseNet169 Model
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Sign language is a crucial means of communication for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, relying on specific signs, hand shapes, gestures, and facial expressions to express ideas and information. Since many deaf individuals face challenges with verbal communication, reading, and writing, developing a Sign Language Recognition (SLR) system is crucial for enhancing their ability to interact with hearing individuals. This paper presents a solution using the DenseNet169 model to recognize American Sign Language (ASL) gestures. We utilized a dataset representing the ASL alphabet, consisting of 24 classes (excluding the letters J and Z, which involve movement), with a The dataset contains 27,455 samples for training and 7,172 samples for testing. It was divided such that 80% of the data was used for training and 20% for testing. The proposed model has achieved impressive results, with a validation accuracy of 98%, highlighting its potential to significantly enhance communication for the hearing-impaired community. This work contributes to the advancement of human-computer interaction by providing an effective tool for recognizing sign language gestures and facilitating communication.

articleTitle: Pepper Berries Graded Using Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The classification of pepper berries is a critical task in agriculture, traditionally graded by manual methods that are prone to inconsistencies, high labor costs, and inefficiencies. This study aims to automate the classification of pepper berries into four distinct grades using advanced deep learning techniques by utilizing various advanced deep learning architectures with a refined DenseNet-151 model. Researchers demonstrate through experiments on a variety of datasets that deep learning approaches significantly improve classification accuracy and efficiency compared with traditional approaches. Due to its effective feature propagation and dense connection the optimized DenseNet-151 model proved to be the best performer obtaining an accuracy of 98%. Furthermore, the models MobileNetV2, Vgg16 and InceptionNet had strong results, achieving 93%, 94% and 94% accuracy while ResNet only managed 87% accuracy. Future work will concentrate on expanding the dataset employing complex techniques of data augmentation and investigating advanced model architectures in order to further improve performance. Validating the practical efficiency of these models and developing precision agriculture and smart agricultural practices will depend greatly on their real-world deployment.

articleTitle: Analysis on Capacity of Next Generation Wireless Communication Networks using Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This research study analyzes next generation wireless communication networks as that of 5G wireless networks using artificial intelligence (AI) such as artificial neural networks(ANN). 5G wireless communication networks comprising of antennas in large numbers play a pivotal role in handling data information traversing in a wireless channel. The metric of capacity analysis in 5G next generation wireless communication network is analyzed in a massive MIMO wireless channel for its signal to noise ratio (SNR) counterpart. The obtained.

articleTitle: Deep U-Net Based Dental Caries Detection and Classification in Panoramic X-Ray Images
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Dental caries, identified as a frequent oral health issue, demands timely detection and classification for effective treatment planning and prevention of further complications. This work focuses on developing a robust automated system to detect and classify dental caries using radiology images of panoramic X-ray. The proposed automated classification system aims to accurately identify the required region of interest and categorize regions of dental caries within images of X-ray using deep convolutional learning methods. The workflow begins with acquisition of raw input images of panoramic X-ray images, containing various stages and types of dental caries followed by finetuning them. Subsequently, a custom-designed CNN architecture (U-Net) is trained on the selected dataset using appropriate loss functions and optimization techniques. Testing image sets are used to evaluate the model, and performance is assessed by accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and other relevant metrics. A maximum of 94% of diagnostic accuracy is reported with appropriate sensitivity and specificity using U-Net based segmented images. The effectiveness related to the developed system is measured in automated finding the regions of dental caries, by minimizing the errors of manual examination by dental professionals. This automated approach holds significant potential for improving diagnostic efficiency, enhancing treatment procedures, and ultimately contributing to better oral healthcare outcomes.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cyberbullying Detection in Social Media: Leveraging Ontology with Skip- Gram Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The pervasive issue of cyberbullying on social media platforms highlights the critical need for robust detection systems to ensure user safety. This research introduces a novel approach to enhance cyberbullying identification by integrating ontology with the Skip-gram optimization technique. The proposed methodology leverages ontological frameworks to identify semantic relationships within social media content, combined with Skip-gram optimization to generate accurate and robust word embeddings. The objective is to improve both the precision and effectiveness of cyberbullying detection. Ontology-enhanced embeddings demonstrate superior performance compared to standard word embeddings when used with an LSTM classifier, as indicated by experimental results. The findings show significant improvements in detecting instances of cyberbullying across various social media platforms. In the rapidly evolving digital landscape, the combination of ontology and Skip-gram optimization offers a promising solution to the complex challenges of cyberbullying detection.

articleTitle: Physics Informed Neural Networks for Reliable SOC Estimation in Lithium-Ion Battery Management
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Physics Informed neural networks is gaining popularity by, providing more reliable SOC estimates as, traditional SOC estimation methods struggle with varying conditions and data quality. This paper presents SOC assessment of Lithium-ion cells integrating physical models and machine learning techniques. An equivalent circuit model has been created and validated through experiments, which is used to produce a substantial dataset, including voltage, current, and temperature measurements. This dataset is generated across a wide range of operating conditions, encompassing different load profiles and temperature variations, and is incorporated into the loss function as part of the NN framework. This innovation is essential for advancing EV technology and meeting the growing demands for efficiency and sustainability. SOC estimation is crucial for optimizing the performance, safety, and lifespan of lithium-ion cells in EVs.

articleTitle: A Cost Effective IoT Based Firefighting Rover
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: In this research study, an IoT-enabled firefighting rover has been fabricated to cater to the growing demand for safe and efficient firefighting operations in hazardous areas. It is fitted with cameras, heat sensors, and water hoses, which permit self-detection of the site of fire and sending of real-time data and video feedback to CPS. Integration of IoT in such a way allows for the process to be remotely operated, hence minimizing human risk while enhancing efficiency. Given the fact that it can manage difficult terrain and act right against fire hazards, the rover proves to be one of the best solutions in terms of safety and effectiveness for firefighting in modern times.

articleTitle: The Role of AI in Identifying Depression: A Review of Techniques and Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Depression affects over 280 million people globally, posing challenges to traditional diagnostic methods due to their subjectivity and time inefficiency. This review examines the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in detecting depression, emphasizing Natural Language Processing (NLP), deep learning, and multimodal techniques. Social media analytics and sentiment analysis are pivotal in early detection, addressing patterns in user behavior and interactions. While AI shows potential, challenges such as privacy concerns, data diversity, and ethical considerations persist. This paper emphasizes the need for robust model validation, improved interpretability, and collaborative frameworks for deploying AI in mental health care.

articleTitle: Cancer Region Segmentation in Pre-Processed Breast Ultrasound Image Using VGG16 Based UNet/SegNet
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Breast Cancer (BC) is a predominant cause of mortality among women globally, with its incidence progressively rising due to various causes. Early detection of BC is crucial to plan and execute appropriate treatment to cure the disease. The clinical level examination of the BC involves in; personal check by the doctor, screening using non-invasive medical imaging modality, and biopsy test to confirm the BC and its stage. Compared to the radiological imaging modalities, the breast-ultrasound (BU) based screening is widely preferred due to its simplicity. The abnormality recorded with BU is then examined to classify the tumor as benign/malignant, an essential process during BC detection. This research aims to propose a deep-learning (DL) tool to segment the tumor from the chosen BU-image. To enhance the segmentation accuracy, every image is preprocessed using tri-level thresholding with Tsallis's Entropy and Hummingbird-Algorithm (TE+HA). The performance of proposed UNet/SegNet is verified on both unprocessed and preprocessed images. The experimental outcome of this research confirms that the VGG-UNet offered an improved mean accuracy (>97<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) when the preprocessed BU is considered for examination.

articleTitle: Utilization of Artificial Intelligence in Electronic Product Design
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Prototyping and the medical field have been transformed by the extensive use of 3D printing. Nevertheless, mistakes can occur during the process, resulting in unsuccessful prints, material waste, and lost time. By providing real-time issue identification and repair, artificial intelligence (AI) provides a solution and revolutionizes 3D printing. In order to identify printing flaws with 97.77% accuracy, this study created a Machine Learning (ML) model using Support Vector Machines (SVM). By enabling automatic modifications, the model's integration into a smart slicing process greatly decreased mistakes, increasing efficiency and dependability. These results demonstrate how AI may improve the precision and efficiency of 3D printing.

articleTitle: An Innovative Regional Condition Hybrid Routing Protocol Accessing in Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The heterogeneous wireless mesh methodologies proffer a chance for increase in capacity of a network and achieve greater quality of service (QoS). Distinct standards, protocols, and access technologies are used in wireless devices. However, the existing research negligent entire way, so RC method based on a combination of WMN is proposed. The base, source of network creates the hybrid wireless mesh network. Multiple radio interfaces are involved in the mesh routers and a technique such as regional condition hybrid routing protocol (RC-HRP) enlarge the volume of a system. The entire proactive path is considered for accessing efficiently, inclusion of gateway-oriented traffic and client-oriented traffic studied completely. The simulation results using ns-3 displays the merits of RC-HRP with regard to latency, throughput.

articleTitle: Models for the Prediction of Cardiovascular Diseases Based on Machine Learning- A Brief Review
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD) causes arterial stiffening and reduced oxygen supply to the heart, posing a significant global health risk. Early detection and treatment are crucial for improving prognosis. This study proposes a non-invasive diagnostic technique using iris images, combining iridology with advanced image processing. Iris regions corresponding to the heart were extracted using integral differential operators and rubber sheet models. Feature extraction methods, including wavelet transforms, statistical analysis, and gray-level pixel matrices, were employed. The model's performance was assessed using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and Area Under the Curve metrics. To enhance CAD prediction, the study addresses challenges like dataset imbalances through machine learning (ML) and deep learning classifiers, including Random Forest, XGBoost, CNN, SVM, Logistic Regression, and KNN. The findings improve predictive accuracy for myocardial infarction and provide insights for developing robust early detection models.

articleTitle: Optimization of Speech Emotion Recognition Through Advanced Ensemble Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Recognition of emotion in speech (RES) is generating significant interest due to its promise to improve human-computer interaction through precise identification of emotions from speech signals. This work investigates how well deep learning methods advance RES accuracy. The study makes it possible to analyze a variety of speech patterns, emotional expressions, and demographic information all of which are crucial for developing trustworthy RES models. According to the study, CNNs demonstrated their ability to capture spatial characteristics from voice spectrogram representations with an amazing accuracy rate of 93%. RNNs performed exceptionally well at modeling temporal dependencies and capturing the sequential nature of speech, with an accuracy rate of 90%. Both models performed well, but some emotions such “angry” and “surprise” were more accurately detected than others, including “disgust” and “happy,” suggesting room for improvement.

articleTitle: RFID-Driven Smart Shopping Trolley
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Shopping is now an integral part of our lives, mainly in cities, as hypermarkets and grocery stores have become a daily haunt for basic supplies. Advanced technology has greatly benefitted the retail industry by offering small and medium-scale enterprises the practicality to adopt smart trolley technology. It brings an increasingly efficient, user-centric, and streamlined shopping experience through the use of sophisticated technologies that address shortcomings and achieve greater overall operational efficiency. The smart cart trolley does scanning the products and enables real-time data updates of the products in the supermarket. The main advantage of the trolley is that it can transfer the information of products and even display the time that they were purchased. The details are displayed on the Thingsboard, which is an open-source IOT platform. Thus, it easily facilitates shopping, enjoys personalized assistance, and the comfort of smart carts besides the long queuing time. The product information is displayed on the LCD screen; this feature attracts the user. It is a high-value asset with applications of technology products such as RFID and IoT. Smart cart trolleys were introduced as an inventory control of real-time products. The initiative was mostly to remove the long queues and provide information to customers.

articleTitle: Solar Cell Defect Detection using Deep-Learning Segmentation with Two-Fold Training
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Recently, the applications of Deep Learning (DL) methodologies have been extensively utilized across numerous areas to extract critical solutions from selected databases. The DL Segmentation Tool (DLST) is frequently utilized to extract and assess selected segments from digital images captured using various modalities. This study intends to propose a DLST to analyze the selected database for the identification of defects in solar cells. The proposed DLST encompasses several phases: (i) image acquisition and resizing, (ii) application of an image preprocessing technique to improve defect visibility, (iii) execution of the segmentation process utilizing a selected DL-model to extract the defect, and (iv) comparison of the segmented region with a binary mask and calculation of performance metrics. The created DLST incorporates the VGG-UNet, with VGG19 serving as the model's backbone. This work implemented a two-fold training approach for improved outcomes. The experimental result is validated using selected image metrics, demonstrating that the proposed DLST yields superior values of Jaccard (91.31%), Dice (95.38%), and Accuracy (96.18%) in comparison to other chosen DL models.

articleTitle: PODX: A Comprehensive Framework for Detecting Prohibited Items in Security X-Rays
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The increasing need for accurate and reliable detection of prohibited items such as guns, knives, and pliers in X-ray security images underscores the importance of advanced frameworks to enhance security screening processes. This study introduces Prohibited Object Detection in X-rays (PODX), a comprehensive two-stage framework aimed at improving detection capabilities through advanced feature extraction and classification techniques. The framework employs a two-stage approach: in the first stage, three convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures-ResNet, GoogLeNet, and DenseNet-are utilized to extract features, which are further refined using LASSO (Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator) regression to select the most significant features for classification. In the second stage, multiple machine learning algorithms, including Random Forests, Gradient Boosting, Support Vector Machines (SVM), and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), are implemented to classify prohibited items based on the refined features. The performance of these algorithms is evaluated using metrics such as train accuracy and test accuracy, providing a comprehensive assessment of their strengths and weaknesses. The PODX framework not only enhances the accuracy and reliability of detecting prohibited items in security applications but also offers valuable insights into the comparative effectiveness of various classification techniques in X-ray image analysis.

articleTitle: Smart Energy Management System using Automatic Changeover and Current Limiter with Voltage Protection
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: An important issue facing power utilities is Automatic Load Control, it is largely responsible for the complex dimensions & structure of the linked power networks. The power system is in charge of ensuring that consumers receive a sufficient amount of dependable, high-quality electricity. A power system's regular load fluctuates because of various loading conditions. As a result, maintaining the frequency and voltage within the prescribed limits is difficult. Automatic Change Over with Current Limiter with Phase Loss and Phase Reversal Protection is the main goal of this research project. This approach provides the best way to maintain the load inside a given range, saves money and energy as a result, lowering the maximum demand. It enables the user to turn ON. It enables the user to continuously switch the load up to the rated current.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Slotted Rectangular Patch Antenna for Dual-Band Radar Applications in C and X Bands
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This work presents the design and analysis of a slotted patch antenna optimized for dual-band radar applications across the C-band and X-band frequency ranges. These frequency bands are essential for radar systems used in applications such as long-range surveillance, weather monitoring, and defense operations. The proposed antenna resonates at three distinct frequencies: 5.26 GHz and 7.62 GHz in the C-band, and 11.60 GHz in the X-band. At 5.26 GHz, the antenna achieves an S-parameter of -19.89 dB, a bandwidth of 240 MHz, a VSWR of 1.76, and a gain of 8.1 dB. At 7.62 GHz, the antenna demonstrates an S-parameter of -24.90 dB, a bandwidth of 160 MHz, a VSWR of 1.00, and a gain of 4.9 dB. In the X-band, the design achieves resonance at 11.60 GHz, with an S-parameter of -23.62 dB, a bandwidth of 900 MHz, a VSWR of 1.14, and a gain of 6.4 dB. The design optimizes antenna performance across both frequency bands, ensuring compatibility with various radar applications.

articleTitle: Detecting IoT Botnets with Advanced Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The widespread use of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has resulted in heightened susceptibilities and the rise of intricate botnet attacks, hence presenting noteworthy security obstacles. This work uses the IoT-POT dataset, a comprehensive source of IoT network traffic data, to investigate the effectiveness of machine learning (ML) techniques, namely Support Vector Machine (SVM), Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), in detecting botnet attacks. To train and assess the previously described models using these features, the dataset must first be preprocessed to extract pertinent features. Performance metrics including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score are used to evaluate and compare the models' efficacy. Early findings demonstrate the potential of ensemble techniques like RF, XGBoost, and LightGBM for real-time detection of breaches in IoT networks since they beat conventional SVM for recognising botnet activity. In addition to offering insights into upcoming advancements in botnet detection techniques, this comparative analysis highlights the significance of sophisticated ML techniques in bolstering IoT security.

articleTitle: Analysis of Cup to Disc Ratio Using Fundus and Optical Coherence Tomography Images
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: In this work involves a two-phase approach for diagnosing glaucoma by calculating the Cup to Disc Ratio (CDR) using both fundus images and Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) images. In first phase, fundus images are used to segment the Optic Disc (OD) using the Fuzzy Local Information C Means (FLICM) clustering method, and the Optic Cup (OC) is detected using the super pixel method. The boundaries of the OD and OC are then used to compute the CDR. In the second phase, OCT images are employed to calculate CDR by segmenting the Retinal Virtual (RV) boundary using a wavelet transform and the Retinal Choroid (RC) boundary using multilevel thresholding. These segmented boundaries are then smoothed using a B-spline curve to compute the CDR. After obtaining the CDR values from both imaging methods, they are validated against each other. It was found that the mean error from the CDR value is smaller in fundus images compared to OCT images, suggesting that fundus images may offer more accurate CDR measurements for glaucoma diagnosis.

articleTitle: Academic Metrics Visualization and Analysis System
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The academic metrics include gathering information from students regarding their classes, the teacher's effectiveness in the classroom, and the student's learning objectives. The creation of a web-based, multi-user system for academic performance and a recommendation system that is reliant on the effectiveness and qualifications of the teacher is the main goal of this research project. With the inclusion of the paperless technique, the system performed better and saw less data loss. A lot of people use visual analytics approaches to make it easier to explore data from online schooling. In order to give academics a more thorough understanding of the application of visualization in online education difficulties, we have conducted a systematic review. Each topic includes a summary of how visual analytics techniques are used and how they help with various analysis tasks. Finally, we address the obstacles and prospects for future research in the application of visual analytics methods to online learning.

articleTitle: Earthquake Prediction Model Using Random Forest and Gradient Boosting Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Accurate earthquake prediction remains a significant challenge in geosciences. This research investigates the application of machine learning algorithms, specifically Random Forest and Gradient Boosting Algorithms, for earthquake prediction. By analyzing historical seismic data, these models aim to identify patterns and predict the likelihood of future earthquake occurrences. This study explores the potential of these machine learning techniques to improve earthquake prediction accuracy and contribute to better preparedness and mitigation strategies for this natural disaster.

articleTitle: Soft Error Analysis on Junctionless RingFET-Based SRAM
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: As CMOS devices are scaled down to smaller geometries, the reduction in gate length makes them more vulnerable to radiation-induced errors and malfunctions. This work uses 3D TCAD simulations to examine the soft error performance of junctionless ringFET based SRAM employing both inner and outer drain arrangements. The effect of an ionizing particle, specifically a heavy ion, is utilized to conduct a single-event upset (SEU) analysis on a ringFET-based 6T SRAM cell to determine the critical radiation dosage, which is the lowest amount of radiation required to alter the cell's contents and flip its state. The simulation results reveal that the linear energy transfer threshold of Junctionless ringFET based SRAM using an inner drain arrangement requires approximately 5.2 times more radiation to cause an error than the Junctionless ringFET based SRAM using an outer drain arrangement.

articleTitle: Decoders for FEC Codes - A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: FEC codes are a specialized type of code designed to detect and correct errors that occur during data transmission, ensuring data integrity. By intentionally introducing redundancy during encoding, FEC ensures that decoders can reliably extract original messages from received data, even if corrupted by transmission errors. This paper offers an overview of diverse decoding methods developed by various researchers.

articleTitle: Analysis of Tapered Microstrip Patch Antenna with Slot Integration at 28 GHz for Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: An innovative antenna design that has been specifically engineered for 28 GHz communication systems is presented in this study. This design was developed to fulfill the demand for high-performance, wideband antennas that are suitable for use in radar and satellite applications specifically. A rectangular microstrip patch with tapered corners and a slot that is strategically positioned is included in the proposed antenna design. This patch is fabricated on a FR4 substrate that is 1.6 mm in height and has a dielectric constant of 4.4. Inset feeding and partial ground plane techniques are utilized in order to optimize the design, using Ansys HFSS software. The antenna exhibits remarkable performance characteristics, including a return loss of −69.5042 dB at a frequency of 27.29 GHz, a Voltage Standing Wave Ratio (VSWR) of 1.0007 at the same frequency, and an impedance matching of 49.98 ohms. In addition, it achieves a notable gain of 5.2 dB and possesses an extensive bandwidth of 5.26 GHz, giving it an advantage over conventional designs in terms of versatility and efficiency. In this study, the effectiveness of the proposed antenna architecture is demonstrated, and the potential of the architecture to improve communication systems of the next generation that operate at millimetre-wave (mmW) frequencies is addressed.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Dynamic Memory Cell Using CNTFET, FINFET and MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: There is a sizable amount of memory built right into every digital device. Dynamic Random Access Memory (DRAM) is the ideal memory when it comes to significant and reasonably priced memory needs. It serves as the fastest main memory. Two important factors that contribute to a quicker and more efficient process are cutting the channel length and reducing leakage currents. There is more control over the current flow from the source to the drain with modern field effect transistors (FET). In this paper, DRAM is designed using MOSFET (Metal Oxide Semiconductor FET), FINFET (Fin Shaped FET) and CNTFET (Carbon NanoTube FET) and made a comparison in terms of power consumption, read and write delays and power dissipation using Cadence Virtuoso tool.

articleTitle: Detection of Deepfake Audio Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Deepfake technology employs AI algorithms to create misleading digital information, such as photos, movies, and audio recordings. Deepfakes can now create realistic-looking content, making detection more challenging. Most studies on detecting audio deepfakes use various machine learning and deep learning algorithms with the ASVSpoof dataset, despite recent advancements in video deepfake detection. MFCCs are used to extract useful acoustic information. The dataset was constructed using a text-to-speech model and then partitioned into a few datasets. Datasets are divided into subsets according to bit rate and audio length. The experimental results demonstrate that support vector machines (SVMs) outperformed other machine learning (ML) models in terms of accuracy. Our objective is to enhance the model's efficiency and detection accuracy through the use of deep learning techniques with CNN and LSTM neural networks. Using Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) as a classifier, that can determine whether audio is real or fraudulent. And a Graphical User Interface (GUI) was further implemented for a better visual representation of the output, that is obtained

Author Keywords: ASVSpoof(Automatic speaker verification spoofing and countermeasures)

articleTitle: Speech Emotion Recognition for Psychiatric Care Using Vision Transformers and Predictive Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Speech emotion recognition is the process of ascertaining and identifying feelings in speech so that machines could better understand human emotional states. SER is also being used in customer service for improving the experience of users, security to identify the threats, and healthcare to track emotional wellness. This complex SER system is designed particularly for psychiatric sessions by using the Multiscale Vision Transformer MViTv2 for detecting the emotions of the patient during therapy. The audio signal is captured and then transformed into Mel Spectrograms using Short-Time Fourier Transform (Mel-STFT) of these spectrograms to be fed into MViTv2 to start extracting elaborate emotional features. These features get classified with the aid of Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), which sums up the emotional status of the patient for the session as a whole. Another subsidiary module, LLM, is utilized in predicting the number of the sessions that may be needed for treatment in the future, giving quite valuable predictive insight to the planning of therapy and enabling proper communication between psychiatrists and patients. Such a system demonstrates excellent robust accuracy over multiple datasets and lays the groundwork for further developments, such as video-based emotion recognition, to make psychiatry even more advanced.

articleTitle: Enhancing Power Conversion Efficiency in WO3-Based Perovskite Solar Cells Through Interface Defect Density Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This study, aiming at optimizing critical parameters including open-circuit voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OC</inf>), short-circuit current density (J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SC</inf>), fill factor (FF), and power conversion efficiency (PCE), this work investigates the effect of interface defect densities (IDD<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> & IDD<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) on the photovoltaic performance of formamidinium-based perovskite solar cells (FA-PSCs) with structure Zn2P3/ (FA)2BiCuI6 /W03. Device efficiency was observed by varying interface defect levels between 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup> and 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ls</sup>fcm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Reducing IDDs greatly increases V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">oc</inf>; it peaks at 1.150 V when both IDD<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and IDD<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> fall between 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup> and 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup> /cm-, In a comparable line, low defect densities recorded the highest J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SC</inf> of 26.48 mAfcm2; larger defect densities caused a consistent decrease in both V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OC</inf> and J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SC</inf> mostly owing to increased charge carrier recombination. Reducing defect densities enabled one to achieve the greatest PCE of 26.12%, therefore highlighting the need of defect management for raising solar cell efficiency. Working with affordable and clean energy, this strategy increases material quality for maximum energy production, therefore allowing the development of more sustainable solar technology. Furthermore advancing greener, more reasonably priced energy for future generations would be aiding. Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure using perovskite solar cells as a scalable and sustainable energy source.

articleTitle: Emerging 6G Services for the Smart Society: Towards Seamless Connectivity
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The era of 6G communication is thought to be the fusion of human being with digital and physical world. The 6G communication have started attracting many industries and academia because of its immense capabilities to drive various application. The evolution of 6G standard can be the advancement of the current 5G standards. It could provide variety of services under a single platform, hence there is a need for robust and reliable architecture that can satisfy various needs at different levels. In this article, we present various 6G services in brief, starting with the different challenge faced at the 6G operating frequencies, to the role of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) to provide these services in effective and efficient manner. It is expected that everything should be connected to every other thing in this new standard, providing the connectivity to remote places is a prime challenge; to address this issue, we have presented the idea of connected ocean through a sample infrastructure diagram.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Security in IoT using Secure Hash Cryptography Algorithm with Double Encryption (SHCA-DE)
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The “Internet of things” is the developing technology to transfer the world into smart innovation. “IoT” security is the most problematic issue in recent applications due to its properties including ‘centralized architecture’, ‘limited capacity devices’, and ‘ambiguity’. So, blockchain with “IoT” applications provides secure data communication compared to traditional “IoT” applications. Blockchain is a recent growing technology that has features including ‘decentralized structure’, ‘transparency’, ‘immutable records’, ‘increased capacity’, and ‘quick backtracks’. The ‘cryptography hash algorithm’ is very important to provide secure data transmission. It converted the different size input to fixed-size unalterable output to enhance the security. But still, it needs efficient algorithm to secure data transmission with safeguard of private key. The objective of this paper is to propose a secure hash cryptography algorithm with double encryption (SHCA-DE) to protect the private key message. Then, this proposed algorithm has been analyzed with MD5, SHA-256, and SHA3-512. From this analysis, the SHA3-512 performs well with proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Interactive Carpentry Training with Augmented Reality Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This research study presents a markerless augmented reality (AR) application that aims to deliver basic carpentry knowledge in an engaging, interactive, and informative learning experience. The application offers users to project the 3D model animations of different necessary carpentry hand tools like hacksaw, carpenter's glue, and hand plane into real-world spaces. Using a simulated but realistic context, user can visualize and practice appropriate tool usage which significantly helps to understand and learn faster. User testing showed that the app increased engagement and improved learning results when compared to traditional methods. The complete outcomes illustrate AR's power in some vocational training. It provides a very practical and affordable way to learn by doing. Future work will include scaling up the tool library and developing supported collaboration to deepen learning processes and extend interaction into more intricate aspects of carpentry.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Deep Learning Approach for Brain Tumor Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Brain tumor presents a significant health concern to a person and this concern emphasize need of a right and prompt diagnosis of the patient for effective medical treatment. Traditional diagnostic methods often rely on invasive procedures and expert interpretation, leading to variability in outcomes. In this decade deep learning research has been remarkable and has left a significant impact on medical domain. This research proposes a hybrid model that integrates multiple convolutional neural networks to enhance the brain tumors classification using MRI images. The proposed model uses the transfer learning with pre-trained architectures (i.e. EfficientNet and VGG16) to improve the feature extraction with minimized extensive training data requirement. By implementing early stopping and data augmentation techniques, the proposed model achieves robust performance and generalization capabilities. The results prove that the hybrid model outperforms existing methods, achieving an accuracy of 99.72% on a comprehensive dataset that has various tumor types. This research contributes in the efforts to develop automated diagnostic systems in healthcare.

articleTitle: The Implementation of Blockchain Technology to Manage Data in a Secure and Transparent Manner for Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This research investigates the application of Blockchain technology to enhance the security, transparency, and efficiency of biomedical data management. By analyzing existing data management practices in the biomedical industry and identifying their limitations, the study explores the potential of blockchain to address these challenges. The research focuses on developing a blockchain-based framework for secure data sharing, leveraging the inherent features of blockchain technology, such as decentralization, immutability, and cryptographic security. Through simulations and case studies, the study evaluates the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed framework in addressing critical issues such as data security, privacy, and interoperability. The findings of this research demonstrate the potential of blockchain technology to revolutionize biomedical data management, enabling secure and efficient data sharing while ensuring patient confidentiality and regulatory compliance. This research has broader implications for other data-intensive sectors, highlighting the potential of blockchain technology to enhance data security and integrity across various domains.

articleTitle: A Novel Deep Learning Technique Based Automatic Detection of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome Using Ultrasound Images
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: One of the most common reasons women can't conceive is a hormonal issue called polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS). Symptoms of polycystic ovarian syndrome include being overweight, having excessive body hair, menstrual irregularities, and acne. Prompt diagnosis is key for successful management of polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS). However, the diagnosis is based on the Rotterdam criterion, which includes factors like high androgen hormone levels, ovulation failure, and polycystic ovaries on ultrasonography (PCOM). The current gold standard for diagnosing polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS) relies on ovary ultrasonography, which requires doctors and radiologists to physically count follicles and determine their volume within the ovaries. This study presents an advanced ensemble-based strategy called Adaptive-Synthetic-Sampling. It uses the cat boost algorithm for feature selection and integrates voting and averaging methods.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review of Multi- Layer Convolutional Sparse Coding in Semantic Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This research study investigates the advancements and performance of Convolutional Sparse Coding (CSC) strategies in semantic segmentation, with a particular focus on the Multi-Layer Convolutional Sparse Coding (ML-CSC) model. The ML-CSC framework integrates traditional U-Net architectures with multi-layer CSC blocks, addressing the limitations of conventional convolutional methods. This paper analyzes how the ML-CSC model enhances semantic and appearance information, promoting faster convergence and improved segmentation accuracy. This review highlights the model's performance across various datasets, including DeepCrack, Nuclei, and CamVid, achieving higher mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) scores compared to traditional U-Net models. The findings underscore the significance of the ML-CSC model in improving feature extraction and segmentation accuracy, marking a substantial advancement in the field. This analysis not only contributes to the understanding of ML-CSC's impact on semantic segmentation but also offers insights into future enhancements and relevant application areas, including medical imaging, urban planning, and autonomous driving.

articleTitle: An Acceptable Deep Learning Approach for Detecting Drowsiness
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This research addresses the critical issue of driver drowsiness, a significant contributor to road accidents. The study proposes a real-time driver drowsiness monitoring system utilizing state-of-the-art deep learning models, including InceptionV3,Xception, and Densenet121 with Transfer Learning. The system analyzes real-time video or image data to detect signs of drowsiness, such as eye closure, yawning, and head tilting. Evaluation results demonstrate that the Xception model with Transfer Learning achieves the highest accuracy (99.36%), followed by Densenet121 and InceptionV3with LSTM. The system aims to enhance road safety by providing real-time alerts to drivers and potentially incorporating countermeasures to prevent accidents caused by drowsiness. This research has the potential to significantly impact road safety and contribute to a reduction in traffic accidents worldwide.

articleTitle: Plagiarism Detection and Similarity Checking Program using Machine Learning and String Matching Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This research proposes a system for detecting plagiarism in academic submissions. The system utilizes advanced text comparison algorithms to identify instances of plagiarism, ensuring academic integrity and promoting a culture of originality among students. By providing educators with a tool to efficiently detect plagiarism, this system aims to streamline the evaluation process and enhance the overall learning experience for students. This system has the potential to significantly reduce plagiarism incidents and foster a more ethical and productive academic environment.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Study on Low Power Novel 1-Bit CMOS Full Adders: Comparative Analysis and Performance Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The continuous advancement of low-power 1-bit full adder designs is a critical factor in the development of modern VLSI systems. This paper presents a comprehensive review of recent innovations in full adder circuits, focusing on hybrid logic, FinFET-based architectures, and Gate Diffusion Input (GDI) techniques. These designs aim to optimize key metrics such as power consumption, propagation delay, and area efficiency, addressing the increasing demand for energy-efficient, high-performance VLSI systems. Hybrid logic approaches, which combine CMOS, PTL, and TGL, demonstrate a balanced trade-off between power and area efficiency, while FinFET-based designs offer superior scalability and control over leakage currents at sub-20 nm technology nodes. GDI techniques, though promising in reducing transistor count and power, face challenges related to voltage degradation, requiring further innovation to maintain robust performance. The analysis highlights the trade-offs inherent in these designs and underscores the importance of the power-delay product (PDP) as a key figure of merit. Furthermore, the paper explores future directions in full adder design, including multi-threshold CMOS (MTCMOS), dynamic threshold MOS (DTMOS), and 3D-IC integration, to further enhance power efficiency and scalability in next-generation VLSI applications.

articleTitle: Deep Learning and Features Fusion for Colorectal Cancer Detection from Histopathology Images
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Modern hospitals have extensively adopted the automatic disease examination methods to detect diseases from biomedical images of selected modalities. These methods reduce the diagnostic burden and enhance detection accuracy. This study seeks to create a Deep-Learning (DL) tool for the analysis of histopathology images related to colorectal cancer (CC). This DL-tool consists of the following stages: image collection and resizing, feature extraction using a selected DL-scheme, feature reduction through 50% dropout and serial feature fusion to create the Fused-Features-Vector (FFV), followed by binary classification and 3-fold cross-validation to validate the results. This study initially examines traditional DL-models for classification using SoftMax. Based on the results, the two best models are selected to generate the FFV. This study examines the features of VGG16 and ResNet101 to produce the FFV, thereby validating the effectiveness of the proposed scheme. The CC detection utilizing the FFV achieved an accuracy exceeding 95%, confirming that the developed scheme yields improved results on the selected data.

articleTitle: Detection of Multiple Radio Isotopes Using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The detection of radioisotopes using a plastic scintillation detector is a significant challenge due to the inadequate spectrum resolution and low cross-sections associated with these detectors in the context of photoelectric absorption. This study presents a method that detects both a single radioisotope and many radioisotopes from the gamma spectrum of a plastic scintillator using a Deep CNN. The spectra were simulated using the Monte Carlo N-Particle Transport Code 6 to establish the training set, while the spectra were measured using a two-inch EJ-200 to generate the test set, including a total of 1440 spectra. The CNN-based system shown here achieves an identification accuracy of 94.5% for a Multiple radioisotope.

articleTitle: Determining the Toxicity of Water After Oilspill using UAV
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Oil spills are one of the most concerning factors affecting the quality of the water. Oil spills can occur for various reasons, and it often result from a combination of human error, equipment failure, and environmental factors. The impact of oil spills on water quality is multi-faceted, involving physical, chemical, and biological processes. Crude oil releases toxic components such as polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and heavy metals into water bodies. Responsibility for cleaning an oil spill in water lies with the polluter or responsible party, who is legally obligated to finance and execute the cleanup. Exposure to hazardous substances during onsite assessments and cleanup activities poses potential health risks, ranging from respiratory issues due to airborne pollutants to skin-related concerns from contact with contaminated materials. Therefore, the toxicity of the water after an oil spill must be checked, and remedial measures can be taken because aquatic life will also be affected. The turbidity sensor is used to determine the quality of the water. The environmental weather information is collected from the barometer sensor. The sensors are fixed in the Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV). The data from the sensor is sent to the ESP32 WROOM 32 microcontroller, which indeed sends the data to the application. The data is visualized so that the condition of the surrounding environment and the toxicity of the water before starting the cleaning process are intimated to the team.

articleTitle: Blockchain Technology in Secure Voting Systems: Enhancing Transparency and Trust
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This research study investigates the application of Blockchain Technology (BT) to enhance the security and trustworthiness of voting systems. The study begins by reviewing existing voting systems, including cryptographic protocols, paper trails, and electronic voting machines, highlighting their strengths and limitations. Subsequently, it explores the potential of BT to address key challenges such as voter fraud and lack of verifiability. Through case studies and empirical evidence, the study evaluates the effectiveness of Blockchain-based solutions in improving the security, transparency, and efficiency of voting processes. This research contributes to the development of more secure and trustworthy voting systems that can enhance democratic participation and ensure fair and transparent elections.

articleTitle: Service Composition in IoT: A Systematic Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is an interconnection of several devices that work together to ease tasks. Cloud services are an integral part of IoT, which augments the functionality of the devices; each device can connect to the required cloud service assigned to the particular device. If the requested task is complex, i.e., cannot be fulfilled by one device or a single cloud service, a collection of services needs to be orchestrated and choreographed to achieve a common task with apt coordination of the services. This paper reviews the existing literature of the service composition approaches and different architectures in IoT and exhibits the comparative analysis of the various techniques and architectures in the contemporary works in the field.

articleTitle: Agricultural Text Classification and Production Prediction using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This paper presented an integrated approach for predicting agricultural crop types and crop production using deep learning techniques. The first part focused on classifying crop types based on agricultural data, utilizing text classification techniques such as Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Units (GRU), and Bidirectional LSTMs (BiLSTM). Two separate experimentations were conducted for text classification. The first experiment combines the numerical features like area and production to predict the seasonal label. In the second experimentation, seasonal, numerical, and categorical features were combined to predict crop types. Additionally, crop production was predicted using deep learning artificial neural network (ANN) model with production volume as target variable. The proposed method demonstrated the potential of the DL algorithms to analyze complex agricultural datasets.

articleTitle: Multimodal Approach for Diabetic Retinopathy Detection Using Deep Learning and Clinical Data Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: A novel multimodal diabetic retinopathy (DR) diagnosis method is proposed that addresses the most common and time-consuming limitations of traditional diagnosis methods. This approach combines deep learning techniques with medical data fusion to integrate retinal images with important measurements such as glucose levels, blood pressure, and diabetes duration. The model uses convolutional neural networks (CNN) for high-level image analysis and multilayer perceptrons (MLP) to process medical data, and achieves fusion through integration. Compared with image-only models, this principle improves performance metrics including optimization, recall, and classification accuracy. Through the use of visualization and therapy, this approach provides large-scale and flexible solutions for many clinical environments. This study demonstrates the various aspects of multidisciplinary work in the diagnosis of DR, paving the way for better patient outcomes and setting a new standard for integration into expert clinical practice in medicine. Future work will focus on expanding the data, developing the translational model and exploring real-world applications.

articleTitle: Analysis of Optical Parameters Through Simulation-based Study of N+Pocket Doped Vertical NC-TFET
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: In the present article, a more sensitive photosensor built on a Vertical Negative Capacitance TFET is designed and analyzed. The photosensor uses a gate stack with an N+ pocket of SiGe in the source area and a silicon-doped Hf02 ferroelectric layer. The device's performance is increased even more by including the SiGe N+ pocket in the source region, which makes the electron injection process more efficient. A decrease in the off-state surface potential is made possible by the gate stack, which comprises silicon-doped Hf02 ferroelectric with a thickness of 1 nm. This effectively prevents electron tunneling from the source region and a shallow off-state current, which further raises the photosensor's signal-to-noise ratio. The source region's integration with SiGe's N+ pocket improves the tunneling and B2B process, enabling effective and regulated carrier transport. This enhances the entire device's functionality and increases the photosensor's sensitivity to light.

articleTitle: Emotion-Driven Cyberbullying Detection: A Hybrid Deep Learning Approach Integrating CNN-LSTM and BERT for Enhanced Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This study presents a novel hybrid deep learning framework for detecting cyberbullying on social media platforms by incorporating both offensive language and emotional sentiment analysis. The proposed model integrates Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) for feature extraction and sequence modeling, along with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) for contextual understanding. By analyzing both explicit harmful content and the underlying emotional triggers, the model effectively identifies subtle forms of cyberbullying that traditional methods often miss. Trained on a multilingual dataset, the framework leverages stacked word embeddings (GloVe + FastText) and achieves high accuracy in detecting emotionally charged cyberbullying. The experimental results demonstrate superior performance with an F1-score of 0.97, outperforming existing models. This approach highlights the importance of addressing emotional sentiment in cyberbullying detection, providing a more comprehensive and effective solution for online safety.

articleTitle: Identification of Credit Card Frauds Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Nowadays, most of the transactions are online due to the high involvement of online sales and purchase purposes. Although these transactions provide convenience to their end user, meanwhile these are also the main cause of fraud in online transactions of credit cards. Nowadays, online fraud transactions hiked in some cities generating interest in this topic of utmost security concern and needs to be addressed. Recent research studies proposed many machine learning techniques to resolve such kinds of issues but still their accuracy needs to be improved. In this research, the Kaggle dataset was used to solve the textual data problem. On the dataset downloaded from Kaggle, few machine learning algorithms have been implemented for research validation. An accuracy of 99.87% was achieved by the proposed research work. The proposed model detects the fraud transaction in earlier stages and will be more beneficial for business firms.

articleTitle: Multi-Factor Authentication System Using Keystroke Dynamics and Biometric Face Recognition with Feature Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This project encompasses capturing and optimizing keystroke and biometric data for user authentications and behavioral analysis. Based on the use of computer vision and machine learning techniques, it captures keystroke patterns and facial features. As for keystroke data, it is collected using the pynput library, which logs key press and release times to calculate the duration of each keystroke that could be analyzed. An OpenCV library's Haar Cascade classifier is used to capture the biometric data, that is facial features, by detecting and extracting facial images through the user's webcam. These facial images are then further encoded in base64 format and are stored as part of the biometric profile of users. The GWO algorithm is further utilized for better feature identification and optimal data to enhance performance. The GWO algorithm progressively enhances the facial feature data to achieve the optimal set of features. All captured data will be in the user's specific folder for privacy and data organization. The system works as an advanced mechanism of multi-factor authentication by combining behavioral biometrics such as keystroke dynamics with physiological biometrics like facial features for better accuracy and security. This project could be applied in fields such as cybersecurity, personal identification, and analysis of user behavior.

articleTitle: Redefining Learning Analysis Through Identity
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Redefining Learning Analysis through Identity, an innovative educational solution integrating identity management, AI-driven content personalization, and predictive analytics. Utilizing a Flutter-based front end and a secure Node.js backend with MongoDB, the platform offers an intuitive, personalized experience for students while providing admins with robust tools for content management and progress tracking. Key features include role based authentication, AI-driven content recommendations, and predictive analytics, supporting both personalized learning paths and proactive academic interventions. This paper explores the platform's capabilities in redefining learning analysis by combining identity- based access with detailed performance metrics, enhancing educational outcomes through actionable insights.
