articleTitle: Opinion Mining for Comment Sentiment Analysis of Social Media
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The increasing influence of social media platforms has transformed how public opinion is shaped and shared. Our work introduces a sentiment analysis system capable of processing comments from major platforms (YouTube, Reddit and Instagram) to classify user sentiments as Positive, Negative or Neutral. The goal is to provide actionable insights into user emotions and trends, helping businesses and organizations improve decision-making in the fields like marketing, brand reputation management and public policy analysis. Our system allows users to input URLs from social media posts, automatically fetching and analyzing the comments. By utilizing Natural Language Processing (NLP) methods and Ensemble Learning Models, our system classifies sentiments to deliver meaningful insights in real-time. To increase classification accuracy, the ensemble learning approach integrates several models, such as Random Forest, Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Logistic Regression. Our system's performance is assessed using parameters such as F1-score, accuracy, precision, and recall to ensure reliability in real-world applications. Through this user-friendly platform, organizations can better understand audience sentiment, enabling more informed, data-driven decisions for improved business outcomes.

articleTitle: Movie Recommendation System using DBSCAN Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This paper presents a movie recommendation system utilizing the DBSCAN(Density Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise) algorithm. Traditional recommendation system mostly rely on collaborative filtering or content based filtering. The proposed system addresses these challenges by leveraging DBSCAN to identify dense regions in user-item interaction space, allowing for more robust recommendations. Our model demonstrates the effectiveness of the DBSCAN based approach, getting higher accuracy and user satisfaction compared to conventional methods.

articleTitle: Filter Performance on Dual Active Bridge DC-DC Converter for Electric Vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Bidirectional Dual active bridge (BDAB) DC-DC converters are a flexible and effective way to change power levels in many situations. They have a wide operating range, high efficiency, and can handle power flow in both directions. Can generate lower output voltage and current ripple compared to traditional DC-DC converters, improving system performance and reducing noise. Offers precise control over the output voltage and current, allowing for better regulation and dynamic response. ∏ filters effectively attenuate the high-frequency ripple present in the output voltage, resulting in a smoother and cleaner waveform. It can help to stabilize the output voltage during transient conditions, such as load changes or input voltage variations. It help to minimize voltage sags that occur when the load current suddenly increases, improving the overall load regulation performance. C filters have a relatively limited bandwidth, During sudden load increases, a C filter may experience voltage sags due to its limited energy storage capacity. It is not be as effective at attenuating higher-frequency components. offer limited control over the output voltage. This can make it difficult to achieve precise regulation or to compensate for variations in the input voltage. Filter and ∏-filter performance are compared. ∏-filter Performing well compared to C Filter and it is well suited for EV Applications.

articleTitle: A Comparative Insight into Machine Learning Strategies for Phishing Website Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Phishing attacks have posed a serious threat to the information security cyber world; where malicious websites try to beguile the actual identity of users. Attackers keep adopting new tactics for phishing sites over a while, making it challenging to detect new phishing sites. It has been based on a comparative study of various machine learning models, such as SVM, RandomForest (RF), CatBoost, Voting Classifier, and Stacking Classifier, toward their classification of phishing and non-phishing sites. Different experiments were performed on the dataset, which consisted of features of URLs. Accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score measure performance. Among the various models used for evaluation, the best-performing classifier was the Stacking Classifier with an accuracy of 97.33%, precision value of 0.9684, recall of 0.9793, and F1 score of 0.9738 for the non-phishing websites. This research study has outperformed the rest against phishing websites with a precision of 0.9785, recall of 0.9672, and F1 score of 0.9728. The ensemble approach due to the strengths of multiple base learners improves the classification performance much more than that of any of the individual base learners. This work realizes that there is a great need for future work based on the effectiveness of stacking techniques in phishing detection, and it has the potential to open the door for methods to enhance real-time detection systems against adversarial threats.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of Multi-Slot Wearable Antenna for Early Breast Cancer Detection at 2.69 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The design and performance evaluation of a multislot wearable antenna for early breast cancer detection are presented in this work. The antenna uses Teflon as the dielectric substrate and operates at 2.69 GHz. The ANSYS HFSS simulator, which includes several slots, is used to assess the design. A 72 mm × 61 mm ×3.5 mm compact design is produced by energizing a rectangle radiating patch with a rectangular feed line. This design increases the operational bandwidth and enhances impedance matching with its entire ground plane and novel inset feed technique. With an outstanding return loss of - 18.1068 dB, the suggested antenna shows effective power transfer and less signal reflection. A voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) of 1.2840 is also attained by the antenna, indicating nearly flawless impedance matching across

articleTitle: A User Guide for Familiarizing with Silvaco-Techmodeler and Silvaco-Gateway Tools
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This article states compact modeling of a simulated or fabricated device using the Silvaco-Techmodeler tool. In the Silvaco-Techmodeler tool, according to the device type, either N-TFT or P-TFT (Thin Film Transistor), the corresponding model is selected, and modeled data is produced, which is mapped with simulated or fabricated data to estimate the accuracy. In addition to this, this model is further imported into the Silvaco-Gateway tool for the realization of circuits. Smart-Spice Simulator resides in this Silvaco-Gateway tool used for analyzing the transient and DC behavior of simulated circuits. These 2 analyses would help with the calculation of parameters such as logic swing, noise margin, inverter gain, propagation delay, verifying the truth table, etc. The magnitude of accuracy mentioned above confirms minimal error between simulated or fabricated data and modeled data. The DC and transient curves would be independent of unwanted peaks and glitches only when high accuracy is evaluated. With the help of Silvaco-Techmodeler and Silvaco-Gateway tools, any simulated or fabricated device can be utilized for compact modeling, followed by circuit simulation and evaluation of parameters. These two tools can be utilized for the realization of various digital circuits, memory circuits, and analog circuits.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Effectiveness of Life-Saving Skull Caps to Reduce Injuries During Crashes on Roads
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Smart helmets integrate advanced technologies to enhance safety and performance across activities such as motorcycling. This paper presents a concise overview of the key features and functionalities of smart helmets, including built-in sensors for impact detection and communication systems for real-time connectivity. Additionally, the abstract discusses the potential benefits of smart helmets in reducing accidents and injuries, improving user experience and fostering a safer environment. Through the integration of cutting-edge technologies, smart helmets represent a promising solution for addressing safety concerns and advancing performance in a variety of uses. There are an estimated two million brain injuries recorded annually, of which 28% are thought to result from motorbike accidents. Motorcyclists are not as safe when riding a bike as they are when driving or riding in a car. These wounds could cause permanent damage or possibly result in death. The World Health Organization (WHO) lists injuries from traffic accidents as the tenth leading cause of mortality worldwide in 2016, and it is expected to rise to the eighth rank by 2030 riders not wearing helmets are the two main causes of the daily rise in traffic accidents. Countless individuals are losing their lives in traffic accidents nowadays. Accidents can be identified by employing smart helmets. Making a smart helmet for accident avoidance is the project's primary goal. If the wearer is wearing a helmet or not, the IR sensor detects it. The distinctive utility of the project is to prevent riders from accidents. Only when the rider buckled the helmet then only the motorcycle's engine would start.

articleTitle: Integrated Face Counting and Quick Response (QR) Object Detection with Voice-Based Alerts: A Smart Vision System
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Visually impaired persons (VIPs) face significant navigation challenges both indoors and outdoors, including difficulty detecting obstacles, locating essential amenities, and orienting themselves in unfamiliar environments. By addressing these challenges comprehensively and inclusively, the lives of visually impaired individuals can be enhanced significantly, fostering their independence, safety, and social inclusion. This paper presents an innovative application designed to assist visually impaired individuals in navigating their surroundings through advanced object and person recognition technologies. Utilizing a combination of machine learning algorithms and QR code scanning, the application enables users to identify the number of people standing in front of them and recognize objects by reading their corresponding QR codes. By converting visual information into audible cues, the application fosters independence and enhances the overall mobility of blind users in various environments. The integration of real-time processing and user-friendly interfaces demonstrates the potential for technology to significantly improve the quality of life for visually impaired individuals.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Survey of Integration of Smart Meters with Renewable Energy Sources
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This research elaborates the understanding the pros, cons, and implications of smart meters and renewable energy. Given the increased emphasis on sustainability, especially in the shift to greener energy solutions, smart meters' role in boosting renewable energy resource utilization is vital. Smart meters provide real-time energy production and consumption data important for energy system upgrades. Their accurate energy monitoring encourages greater utilization and energy savings. By combining solar panels and wind turbines, smart meters may minimize fossil fuel use and improve clean energy distribution and consumption. Integrating smart meters with renewable energy is difficult. Efficiency in data management, cybersecurity, and technology interoperability is needed. Poor infrastructure may hinder adoption due to financial and legal constraints. Smart meters on renewable energy sources are promising. Smart meters and decentralized energy system architecture will improve, allowing peer-to-peer energy trading. Community renewable energy utilization may boost energy efficiency and grid resilience, enabling a sustainable energy future. Energy providers, policymakers, and consumers must understand these dynamics.

articleTitle: Resource Allocation and Secure Channel Model for Service-Dependent Mobile Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Channel and resource allocation in mobile edge computing poses a significant challenge for service providers, greatly impacting the quality of service (QoS) in wireless networks. To handle this issue, variety of solutions has been named in literature but still suffer to achieve higher QoS metrics. This article presents a Service-Dependent Secure Channel Allocation and Resource Utilization Model (SSCARUM) aimed at maximizing the Quality of Service (QoS) in wireless networks. The method focused on allocating channel and enforces security according to the service nature. To perform this, the method discovers the channel characteristics like availability, capacity, mean utilization, throughput in various channels. Accordingly, the edge server collects the set of channels available to reach the service points based on the service claimed. With the channels identified, above mentioned factors are collected and estimates Service Completion Support (SCS), Throughput Maximization Support (TMS), Secure Communication Score (SCoS) for various channels. Based on these values, the method calculates the Channel Allocation Score (CAS) to facilitate channel selection and resource allocation. The objective of the proposed work is to develop a Service-Dependent Secure Channel Allocation and Resource Utilization Model (SSCARUM) that optimizes channel selection and resource allocation based on service-specific characteristics, enhancing Quality of Service (QoS) in wireless networks. The model ensures efficient throughput, security, and service completion in mobile edge computing.

Author Keywords: Service-Dependent Secure Channel Allocation and Resource Utilization Model (SSCARUM)

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Aquaculture: Classifying Fresh and Infected Fish using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: With great relevance in preserving the quality of fish in aquaculture and food sectors, this work focuses on the classification of fresh and sick fish using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). Early detection of diseased fish can help stop the spread of illness, thus enabling sustainable consumption and guaranteeing better fish supply, so boosting food security. Developing a strong model for fish categorization is not only relevant but also timely for excellent health and well-being given the growing dependence on automated systems in quality control procedures. This work used a dataset including 305 PNG pictures, split in 90% for training and validation (274 photos) and 10% for testing (31 images). With these data, the CNN model learned to differentiate fresh from sick fish. The generalizing capacity of the model was tested using random images. With an outstanding 94% accuracy on the test set, the model proved successful in identifying fish depending on their health state. This great degree of accuracy emphasizes CNN s' ability to automatically detect sick fish, therefore enabling sustainable aquaculture methods and enhancing food safety.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Mobile Application for Disease Identification in Tomato Leaf
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This research focuses on developing a mobile application for early detection of common tomato leaf diseases using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). Early disease detection is crucial for mitigating crop losses and ensuring sustainable agricultural practices. The application allows farmers to capture images of tomato leaves using their mobile devices, and the CNN model analyzes these images to identify diseases such as Leaf Mold, Two-Spotted Spider Mites, Late Blight, Septoria Spot, Bacterial Spot, Mosaic Virus, and Early Blight. This user-friendly mobile application empowers farmers to quickly and accurately diagnose plant diseases, enabling timely intervention and improving crop yields. This research contributes to the advancement of precision agriculture by leveraging technology to enhance disease management and improve agricultural productivity.

articleTitle: Design of Area Effcient Multiplier Using High Speed 15-4 Counter
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The high-speed counters are the building blocks to reduce the partial products, increasing the efficiency and speed of the multiplier. This paper presents an innovative approach to designing a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$16 \times 16$</tex> multiplier using a 15–4 counter that utilizes cross-wired 1ogic(CWL) based 3–2 counter instead of traditional full adders. A 15–4 counter is designed by employing a 5–3 counter and a CWL-based 3–2 counter to reduce circuit complexity. Using multiple 5–3 counters instead of conventional full adders reduces the computational effort, strategically integrating these 15–4 counters within specific multiplier columns, achieving greater area efficiency and speed. This method addresses the high computational demands associated with adders, optimizing both performance and area in high-speed multiplier applications. From the simulation result, it can be inferred that the proposed 15–4 counter and cross-wired logic 3–2 counter has excellent efficiency, and the power and delay product(PDP) has reduced by 3.6 % when compared to the existing 15-counter design and 30.27 % decreased in the 3–2 counter design,

articleTitle: Computer Vision Based Crop Yield Prediction for Precision Agriculture Using Machine Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Precision agriculture methodologies, which integrate digitalization and automation, are driving a revolution in agriculture through the use of computer vision technology. This intelligent agriculture could also address significant global issues such as food security and sustainability. Advancements in computer and machine vision have significantly improved the detection, quality assessment, and yield estimation processes for various fruit crops; nevertheless, there are yet no completely established systems capable of generating an accurate yield map for vegetable crops. The objectives of a machine vision-based yield monitor were the classification of size (count) and the continuous enumeration of agricultural produce. The proposed system employs a linear regression machine learning model for feature selection and decision tree machine learning model to predict healthy crop yields and provide the optimal framework for implementing completely autonomous farms in real time. The performance of the proposed machine learning model is accessed by Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and R-squared (R2) ranking scores.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator
Author Keywords: Image acquisition and Mean absolute error

articleTitle: Yoga Pose Detection and Correction Using 3D Pose Estimation and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Yoga is an ancient Indian practice that nurtures and enhances both physical and mental well-being. However, performing yoga poses incorrectly can lead to adverse health effects. Many practitioners lack sufficient knowledge of the poses or fail to follow proper instructions, creating a need for a system that can accurately classify yoga poses and offer corrective guidance. This research aims to integrate technology with yoga to assist individuals in performing poses correctly, thus reducing the risk of injury and enhancing the effectiveness of their practice. Specifically, the objective is to detect live, performed yoga poses and provide real-time assistance using the Mediapipe library and deep learning techniques, such as the multilayer perceptron model. Recent advancements in computer vision and deep learning, including pose estimation algorithms and convolutional neural networks (CNNs), have shown promise in yoga pose recognition. However, challenges persist, such as accurately identifying complex and dynamic poses, dealing with variations in body shapes and postures, and ensuring real-time feedback. The proposed system seeks to overcome these challenges by leveraging robust pose detection methods and providing corrective suggestions to improve performance. This research marks a significant advancement in the fusion of technology with wellness, offering innovative solutions in the evolving field of mind-body fitness.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Network Anomaly Detection for Enhanced Cybersecurity and Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Threats of the network that have ever/never happened could be anomalies. Protecting networks against malicious access has always been challenging and despite a long time study into this matter, it never becomes easier. Because of the evolutionary step of the network through new technologies as well as fast growth of connected devices, attacks on the network are getting versatile too. Compared to conventional intrusion detection methods, machine learning is a new flexible approach to detect intrusions in the network and applicable to any kind of network structure. This paper discusses the challenges of anomaly detection in both the traditional network and the next generation network. The implementation of machine learning in anomaly detection under various network contexts. The process of every machine learning class is defined and the methodologies along with the advantages. A summary of the comparison of which uses different models of machine learning in the process is also presented.

articleTitle: AR-Based Learning Tool for Understanding Light Dependent Resistor
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This work presents the development of an augmented reality (AR) application with educational purpose to teach students LDRs working in an electrical circuit. The marker-based AR application visualizes key circuit components in 3D models that user can pan, tilt, and zoom into. After setting up the markers it simulates the working of circuit like turning on a virtual torch, causing LDR to get light this in turn simulates current flow and Bulb glowing. This application provides students with an intensive, practical learning experience that will allow them to better understand the functioning of LDRs in real circuits. Initial tests revealed that the AR tool increased student understanding and engagement compared to more traditional teaching methods. Future developments include investigating markerless AR for more accessibility, enhancing marker identification, and broadening applicability to more complicated circuits. The findings of this research highlight the use of AR technology in aiding accessibility and engagement with abstract physics concepts by students.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Performance of Ensemble Machine Learning Algorithms for Predicting Loan Eligibility
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Loans are becoming increasingly important in the banking sector, but traditional methods of assessing them based mainly on asset value and income often fall short in identifying reliable borrowers. Our research addresses this gap by using machine learning techniques to predict loan eligibility more effectively. We apply algorithms such as Decision Tree, Extra Trees, XGBoost, and LightGBM, with LightGBM achieving an optimal accuracy of 98.91%, to analyze data and produce more accurate predictions. We also introduce a new feature that allows users to input branch-specific details, enabling customized loan assessments based on different bank criteria within each branch. This feature helps users identify banks most likely to approve their loan applications. After predictions are made, the platform displays the locations of the relevant bank branches. Our system allows users to apply for loans online and provides detailed information on various loan types and branch-specific requirements. This streamlined approach reduces loan defaults, accelerates approvals, and offers clients more suitable credit options tailored to their financial circumstances.

articleTitle: Hand Gesture Recognition Using EfficientNetB5: A Robust Approach for Real-Time Human-Computer Interaction
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Human-computer interaction depends on hand gesture recognition, which has a major influence on virtual reality, robotics, and assistive technology among other domains. This work investigates the EfficientNetB5 convolutional neural network model's application to precisely categorize eight unique hand gestures: closed fist, finger circle, finger symbols, multi-finger bend, open palm, semi-open fist, semi-open palm, single finger bend. Drawn from Kaggle, the dataset consists of 1,841 photos guaranteeing a varied depiction of motions to improve model training. Data preparation, model architecture building, k-fold cross-valuation-based training, and performance evaluation comprise the suggested approach. Our findings show a good general accuracy of 90%, with perfect categorization achieved from particular gestures. Particularly in identifying more complicated motions, a classification report and confusion matrix analysis exposes the strengths and opportunities for development of the model. The results highlight the possibilities of EfficientNetB5 in real-time hand gesture detection systems, hence advancing understandable human-computer interactions.

articleTitle: Pre-Frontal Electrode-Based EEG Analysis for Classifying Specific Learning Disability using Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Specific Learning disability (SLD) occurs when a person struggles to read, write, interpret, and spell. Reading and attending normal classes is challenging for children with SLD. Therefore, early detection and classification of SLD children from normal children is essential to improve the quality of life for SLD children. The main objective of the present study is to propose a model to classify SLD children from normal children based on identifying the dominant brain regions from their electroencephalography (EEG) findings. This study uses EEG signals from Fp1 and Fp2 regions to analyze the difference in brain activity between SLD and non-SLD children. This study included 12 SLD and 12 non-SLD children with an age group of 3–14 years. Processing of raw EEG signals, which were taken from the children, was performed using Lab Viewsoftware which involves extracting information from different frequency bands- alpha, beta, delta, gamma and theta bands. The extracted information includes the relative power and relative phase of each band. This study uses Statistical analyses such as Mann Whitney U test, Wilcoxon signed rank test and Friedman test to classify SLD children from normal children. The statistical analyses showed a significant difference between SLD and non-SLD children in Beta Phase of Fp2 region which is used in classifying the SLD children using Machine Learning approach. The classification model uses support vector machine (SVM) with linear, cubic, radial basis function (RBF) and sigmoid kernels. The Machine Learning model had a maximum accuracy of 80% using RBF-SVM classifier.

articleTitle: CNN Architecture for Sclerosis Detection in MRI Data Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This study investigates Convolution Neural Network (CNN) architectures for the detection of sclerosis in MRI data using deep learning techniques, with a focus on implementation in Tensor Flow. Sclerosis detection in MRI is crucial for early diagnosis and treatment planning in neurological disorders such as multiple sclerosis. It evaluates several CNN architectures tailored for this task, leveraging the rich spatial information inherent in MRI scans. The architecture uses a convolution layer to perform feature extraction from images, pooling layers for spatial reduction, fully connected layers for classification, and it also explore mechanisms based on attention to boost model performance, focusing the interest regions. Additionally, it investigates the benefits of deep learning from trained models to expedite training and improve generalization performance. Through extensive experimentation and evaluation on benchmark datasets, it proves that our suggested structures are capable of correctly identifying sclerosis in MRI data. The implementations in Tensor Flow offer scalable and efficient solutions, paving the way for automated sclerosis detection systems integrated into clinical workflows for improved patient care and outcomes.

articleTitle: Benchmarking Machine Learning Algorithms for CAD Prediction using Statistical Tests
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD) remains a major global health challenge, emphasizing the need for accurate and reliable diagnostic tools. This study benchmarks several machine learning (ML) models, including Support Vector Machines (SVM), Naive Bayes (NB), Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest (RF), k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), AdaBoost, Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), and a Mixture of Experts Ensemble combining SVM, KNN, RF, and AdaBoost, for CAD prediction across five datasets: Cleveland, Statlog, Kaggle Framingham, Z-Alizadeh Sani, and JIPMER. Robust statistical tests, including Friedman rank, Iman-Davenport p-value, and post hoc analysis, validate model performance and highlight significant differences. The results reveal the superior performance of the Mixture of Experts Ensemble, demonstrating enhanced accuracy and reliability compared to individual models. However, computational cost and dataset variability pose practical challenges. This work contributes to CAD diagnostics by providing a systematic evaluation framework, ensuring model robustness and generalizability across diverse patient populations.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Logic-Driven Approaches to Enhancing Hardware Security in IoT Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The rapid growth of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has revolutionized various industries but has simultaneously amplified vulnerabilities in hardware security. This paper proposes a fuzzy logic-driven approach to enhance hardware security in IoT devices by addressing critical challenges such as tampering, side-channel attacks, and unauthorized access. The methodology defines key input parameters, including power consumption, temperature variations, and authentication anomalies, while producing adaptive output variables such as security breach likelihood and response intensity. By leveraging the uncertainty-handling capabilities of fuzzy logic, the framework dynamically assesses threats and applies real-time responses to improve security without compromising device performance. The proposed system offers significant improvements in detection accuracy, reduces false positives, and ensures computational efficiency, making it suitable for resource-constrained IoT environments. Validation through simulations highlights the system's ability to balance security and performance, providing a scalable and reliable solution for safeguarding IoT ecosystems.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Brain Tumor Detection Using Deep Learning Models for Enhanced MRI Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Brain tumors cause serious threats to the patient's health that infect the cells within the brain. It causes the growth of abnormal cells. If it is not diagnosed at an earlier stage, it causes severe neurological complications and increases the death rates. Although MRI and other imaging techniques are frequently used to diagnose and classify brain tumors, such as low early-stage accuracy, and high computational requirements. The proposed framework emphasizes the deep learning ability to improve early detection, a significant step toward better patient outcomes through timely and accurate interventions. In this project, four deep learning models such as ResNet50, DenseNet169, Inception V3, and VGG16 are performed. It helps us work with the identification and classification of brain tumors from MRI techniques. Our proposed model shows that the ResNet50 model has an accuracy of 99% when compared with other models. ResNet50 models show the potential to make a non-invasive process with almost the highest accuracy in brain tumor diagnosis. The proposed framework emphasizes the deeplearning ability to improve earl y detection, a significant step toward better patient outcomes through timely and accurate interventions.

articleTitle: Enhancing Lung Cancer Detection and Segmentation Using Advanced Clustering Algorithm for Sustainable Healthcare Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Detecting lung cancer early is vital for increasing survival rates. This paper explores the use of clustering techniques, particularly K-Means and Fuzzy C-Means, to segment lung cancer areas in CT images. Additionally, the study presents modifications to these algorithms aimed at improving their accuracy and performance in identifying tumors. By emphasizing accurate segmentation and reliable diagnostics, the proposed method shows a notable enhancement in the overall detection of lung cancer, leading to more effective and precise diagnostic strategies.

articleTitle: Microstrip Patch Antenna Design Based on Nature Inspired Optimization Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This article presents design and optimization of Microstrip Patch Antenna applying two distinct nature-inspired techniques viz. Firefly Algorithm (FA) and Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) using MATLAB. The target of the optimization techniques is to find minimized resonant frequency mismatch of antenna. Four important design parameters considered here are height, length, width and dielectric constant. Both the techniques are implemented in MATLAB to identify optimal values of all the four parameters, which have been used in designing microstrip patch antennas in MATLAB. The Design 1 is based on Firefly Algorithm and Design 2 is based on Grey Wolf Optimization. Optimization results exhibit that FA converged faster towards solution while GWO tends to achieve lesser final objective function value, delivering a better frequency match. The designs depicted by either algorithm are evaluated for key performance metrics, comprising of resonant frequency, return loss, bandwidth and radiation patterns.

articleTitle: ResNet50-Based Deep Learning Model for Early Detection and Classification of Mango Leaf Diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Mango is not only considered to be the “king of fruits” for its delicious, incomparable taste but is also economically important fruit throughout the world. But mango is susceptible to a number of serious diseases which seriously affect fruit quality and yield. The major diseases of mango leaves include: Anthracnose, Bacterial Canker, Die Back, Gall Midge, Powdery Mildew, and Sooty Mould. By detecting them in an early stage, it can save crops from widespread damage and ensure better fruit production. Conventional detection methods of mango leaf diseases are cumbersome, time-consuming, and prone to human error. In this perspective, the research will seek to apply a class of Conv Net algorithms, a deep learning branch of artificial intelligence characterized by high accuracies realized in image classification tasks, in attempts to meet this challenge. In particular, this study aims at designing an efficient automated system capable of classifying mango leaf images into seven classes with high accuracy value, comprehensively including healthy and diseased leaves. It considers the target for achieving a 95% classification accuracy with the purpose of ensuring a dependable early detection of the disease. This dataset consists of images of mango leaves infected with the above-mentioned diseases, where CNN models are trained to recognize patterns indicative of each condition. The model will help reduce the manual effort involved in the identification of diseases, thereby facilitating timely intervention, which is very important to maintain better mango production. Results obtained show very promising accuracy levels; hence, a favorable solution is offered for farmers and other agricultural stakeholders in managing mango leaf diseases efficiently.

articleTitle: Water Quality Evaluation using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Maintaining the water quality is vital for environmental sustainability,public health, and effective resource management. This research study outlines the development and deployment of a real-time water quality monitoring system., highlighting the essential parameters like pH., turbidity,and hardness. Machine learning algorithms,such as Random Forest(RF),K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN),and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) are utilized to improve prediction accuracy and enable real-time water quality assessment. The water quality managements system has two parts namely the embedded hardware unit with sensor modules, and a machine learning models offers a scalable,cost-effective solution for real-time water monitoring,significantly improving the detection of contamination and enabling efficient water management across various applications.

articleTitle: Enhanced Skin Disease Detection Using Deep Learning with Fully-Convolutional Residual Networks and Lesion Index Calculation Unit
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Detection of skin diseases is a very important branch of medical image analysis and, hence, early diagnosis is vital for the patient's recovery. This paper proposes an integrated multi-stage pipeline of deep learning for automated skin lesion analysis, which includes lesion segmentation, coarse classification, and refined classification using a Lesion Index Calculation Unit (LICU). The segmentation stage precisely segments the lesion, which has a high boundary accuracy of 95%, thus, data that are restricted to real sections could be analyzed. The coarse classification stage is a preliminary step of disease probability, but it has a high tendency for false positives. The LICU refinement stage not only removes these overdiagnoses but also increases the sensitivity by 0.92 and improves the accuracy to 92<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, thus, precision in lesion detection is successfully achieved. Quantitative metrics such as sensitivity, specificity, and the time it takes to process the data, verify both the robustness and the speed of the model. The qualitative analysis also proves that the refined classification stage is more accurate and therefore goes beyond lesion boundaries, which is essential for clinical diagnostics. This multi-step technique not only sharpens the doctor's tools for recognizing the disease but also offers a model that can be easily interpreted thus facilitating doctors in the analysis of complex cases such as skin conditions. In addition, the proposed pipeline is useful in the clinical sector by enabling precise and faster skin disease diagnosis, according to our experiments.

articleTitle: Improved Energy Efficient Divergent Path Routing for Energy-Harvesting Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Since packets are dropped when there is an insufficient connection between each of the sensor nodes in the network, a sensor node in a sensor network is unable to efficiently aggregate the data packets. Since each area has a different sensor node location, the sender node rarely shares information with its neighbour. Only a certain number of packets are received for each communication, the rest are dropped, and the communication is lost. In order to determine each node's minimum residual energy level, the node transmits packets on the path once more. It raises the energy consumption and packet loss rate. Energy-efficient packet aggregation along the network environment is the goal of the suggested Improved Energy Efficient Divergent Path Routing (IEEDP) technique. The node's position is clearly tracked before a different route is assigned for routing. Using metrics such as end-to-end delay, overhead for communication, packet delivery ratio, link stability, consumption of energy, packet loss, and network lifetime using a simulation model, the suggested improved energy efficient divergent path routing (IEEDP) approach outperformed existing methods like Wireless Access Range (WAR) and Congestion-Aware Clustering And Routing (CCR). Energy preservation is a process to extend the network's lifetime by examining the residual Energy Effects on EH-WSN. The Combining Packet Aggregation algorithm is made for sensor networks and collects data packets without any loss during the entire transmission period from the origin node to a target node in a network environment. It lowers energy consumption and packet loss rate.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Low Power Differential Amplifier in SRAM Memory Using Sleepy-Keeper Leakage Control Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This paper presents the design and analysis of a low-power differential amplifier using the Sleepy-Keeper leakage control technique. The rising demand for portable electronics has intensified the need for energy-efficient circuits, especially in digital and analog applications where power consumption is a critical constraint. Differential amplifiers, being a core component in analog and mixed-signal circuits, are susceptible to leakage currents, especially in low-power and high-speed applications. This leakage can significantly impact the performance and battery life of portable devices. The Sleepy-Keeper technique, which combines a “sleep transistor” approach with a “keeper” circuit, aims to minimize leakage power without compromising the performance or stability of the amplifier. By effectively controlling the sleep mode operation during idle states, this technique reduces the leakage current, thereby lowering the overall power consumption of the differential amplifier. The proposed design utilizes complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) technology, enabling the implementation of low-power operations in a highly scalable architecture.

articleTitle: Fire Fighting Robot Using Arduino UNO
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Firefighting robot using Arduino uno project introduces the design and execution of a firefighting robot, focusing on its operational aspects and capabilities for fire suppression. The proposed robot aims to enhance firefighting capabilities in hazardous environments such as fire breakouts while ensuring the safety of human responders. The system consists of an Arduino UNO microcontroller interfaced with various sensors and motors, enabling the robot to navigate within a fire-affected area. Additionally, Bluetooth connectivity facilitates remote control and monitoring of the robot's operations via a software interface. The manual control mode allows operators to intervene and adjust the robot's movement as necessary, providing flexibility and adaptability in firefighting scenarios. The combination of hardware and software allows for quick feedback, improving situational awareness to suppress fires better. The robot shows potential effectiveness and reliability for application in real-world firefighting situations.

articleTitle: Categorization of Alzheimer's Disease and Memory Loss by Using Fusion of Feature Reduction and Kernel SVR
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Physicians often face challenges in determining the significance of a patient's memory difficulties. Aging individuals who notice a decline in their memory are frequently worried about the possibility of developing Alzheimer's disease (AD). Mild memory Loss is a medical condition where cognitive impairment, typically in the memory domain, is present but does not meet the criteria for dementia. Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) is a technique used to assess brain functional abnormalities. In this study, pre-processing is applied to eliminate noise and correct parameter variations in the captured images. Edges are detected, and contours are removed. Regions of grey and white matter, along with gyri and sulci contours, are segmented from the images, and the area and volume of these segmented regions are calculated. The extracted features are then labeled and used in a feature selection process to reduce dimensionality. To categorize Alzheimer's disease (AD), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and normal cognitive function using rs-fMRI data, a structured approach can be used. A kernel-based tSNE method is proposed for dimensionality reduction. For the classification of AD and mild cognitive impairment (MCI), a polynomial kernel-based Support Vector Regression (SVR) is employed.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Stock Price Prediction Using Sentiment Analysis from News Articles
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: In today's world predicting stock prices remains a challenge due to markets being volatile as it is driven by multiple factors. In the past, investors and business men depended on traditional methods of prediction, only taking pre-historic data for consideration. With the addition of introducing new factors that influence today's market and one that is highly overlooked is the market sentiment. Public perception always played a huge role in influencing the market and is crucial for investors to understand the height of the situation. Thus, exploring new areas that were previously neglected is quite the challenge. By introducing algorithms that gain a sentiment understanding from public media combined with various learning algorithm has proved the effectiveness of external factors that playa role in stock price fluctuations. Using a combination of algorithms such as FinBERT for sentimental analysis paired with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) has scored a predictive accuracy of 95%. Other algorithms that have proved notable performance are XGBoost, Gated Recurring Unit (GRU) and DeepAR.

articleTitle: Design Conversion of GPDK 180nm to GPDK 45nm
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Design conversion between different technology nodes, such as from GPDK 180nm to GPDK 45nm, offers nu-merous issues due to differences in device properties, layout and schematic compatibility, operating voltages, and process-specific intellectual property (IP) constraints. Despite the advancement of predictive technology models (PTMs) and the use of advanced synthesis tools and process design kits (PDKs), establishing consistent performance and preserving design integrity across nodes remains difficult. Key problems include ensuring that device characteristics and layout properties are compatible across nodes. Recent approaches, like the ASAP7 for FinFET standard cells, provide advancements; however, there are still constraints in inter-node compatibility and dependability when scaling. This work provides a systematic design conversion approach that addresses these problems through detailed characterization investigations, parameter mapping, and device translation, with a focus on assuring a smooth transition and functionality retention. This technique seeks to improve cross-node design compatibility and broaden the usability of semiconductor designs to consumer electronics and industrial applications.

articleTitle: Fine-Tuning Gemma-2B for Text-to-SQL Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Through this study, the concept of large language models (LLM) in the context of generative AI has been explored. Gemma-2B, with 4-bit quantization is fine-tuned to bridge the gap between natural language processing (NLP) and SQL query generation. The 4-bit quantization significantly reduces memory requirements, making Gemma-2B more efficient for real-world applications while maintaining the performance of the large language model. Users can interact with databases intuitively through simple, text-based inputs. This model employs zero-shot learning, enabling SQL query generation for text descriptions without specific examples in training. Developed and tested within a Google Colab environment, this approach simplifies data retrieval by transforming unstructured language into structured queries through generative AI.

articleTitle: Fleet Management System for Electric Buses using ESP32 Microcontroller
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This research study introduces a comprehensive fleet management system for electric buses, leveraging the capabilities of the ESP32 microcontroller and IoT technology. The system integrates various sensors to monitor key parameters: GPS for real-time bus location tracking, voltage and current sensors for battery health assessment, a speed sensor for velocity regulation, and temperature and vibration sensors for evaluating vehicle performance. Data from these sensors is displayed on an LCD screen and transmitted in real-time to a cloud-based platform, such as Google Sheets, for centralized monitoring and analysis. An intelligent alert mechanism, featuring a buzzer and LEDs, notifies operators of critical conditions, while an automated relay system initiates emergency shutdowns if safety thresholds are breached. The system aims to optimize fleet management, improve operational efficiency, reduce maintenance costs, and ensure the safe, reliable, and sustainable operation of electric buses within a modern transportation network.

articleTitle: Enhancing White Blood Cell Detection in Microscopic Images Through Segmentation and Fusion Methodologies
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: In this study, the IDB2 (acute lymphoblastic leukemia-image database) dataset is used to develop an automated method for distinguishing between leukemia and leukemoid reactions from blood smear images. The approach involves using FLICM (Fuzzy Local Information C-Means) and an active contour model to segment the region of interest in the images. Once the segmentation is complete, wavelet transform-based fusion rules are applied to enhance the segmented output. For classification, VGG19 and MobileNetV3 models are employed to identify whether the sample is in a normal or abnormal stage. The algorithm is designed and executed using Python, with Google Colab providing the necessary computational power and collaborative tools.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of an Intelligent Solar-Powered Street Lighting System with IoT Integration for Enhanced Energy Efficiency and Adaptive Control
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The project aims to create sustainable urban infrastructure by implementing a comprehensive system for highway street lighting using renewable energy sources, particularly solar panels. The system uses a NodeMCU microcontroller for real-time control, enabling remote monitoring and control. Solar panels are strategically used to charge a battery, ensuring efficient energy consumption and minimal impact on generation. The paper presents an IoT-based smart street light system using the ESP8266 microcontroller, LDR, and IR sensor. The system improves energy efficiency and adaptive control, reducing energy consumption and enabling automatic lighting management. The NodeMCU microcontroller, LDR, IR sensors, breadboard, LEDs, and wiring are integrated into a smart street lighting system. The Arduino IDE for programming ensures seamless integration and efficient management. The system eliminates limitations of traditional lighting systems, such as inefficiency and energy consumption, making it suitable for high-traffic areas.

articleTitle: Enhancing Power System Protection with Prediction of Inertia Constant and Frequency Deviations using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This paper explores how machine learning can improve power system protection by predicting critical parameters such as inertia constants and frequency deviations. In the current era, various power systems are consistently integrating renewable energy sources, hence, maintaining the stability of the system has become complex. This study analyzes two configurations i.e. a conventional grid and a microgrid. Machine Learning models are applied to predict frequency deviations and inertia variations under different operating conditions. By forecasting system responses to disturbances, the proposed approach aims to provide timely insights into potential frequency shifts and stability needs. This predictive framework aims to equip power systems with greater resilience and adaptability, addressing the challenges posed by modern grid demands and the variable nature of renewable energy sources.

articleTitle: Utilizing AI for Enhancing Diabetes-Related Quality of Life: A Systematic Review of Measurement Tools
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: It is significant to estimate the extent to which chronic disease management makes a contribution to human health employing the quality of life as a health outcome. The first aim was to conduct a comprehensive analysis of the content and measurement of all those instruments that are focused on diabetes-specific HRQOL. That is why in the present work we adhere to the requirements of Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses (PRISMA). A systematic strategy was used to isolate studies that contain indexes of HRQOL for diabetic patients. A total of 17 instruments were identified in the review that we anticipated our included studies may have used to assess diabetes-specific QOL: Self-completed assessment questionnaires such as Appraisal of Diabetes Scale (ADS), Audit of Diabetes-Dependent QOL measure of a similar kind, Problem Areas in Diabetes PAID questionnaire along with Welfare Monitoring Questionnaire as part of standardized survey London General Practice Group Study Rehabilitation Health Profile 1 Poorly Controlled Hypertension. A total of 17 instruments were included in the review: For diabetes self-management, some recommended measures are; Appraisal of Diabetes Scale (ADS), Audit of Diabetes-Dependent QOL measure (ADDQOL), including ADDQOL version I, II, and III. There are six components and tools in ADAQ, which were regarded as one tool for all types of surveys based on the specified inclusion criteria; ADDFRMS is a short form of MINI Addqol with proper validation and accuracy as compared with full length added but made specially since the last two years by the significant difference between both versions distribution, Diabetes Health Profile (DHP); Problem Areas in Diabetes (PAI-D), “Well-being/Quality.[2] We found seven reviews that assessed a more advanced Structure Drawing methodological aspects aggregation of available scores; however, the review defaulted slightly due to including most of the listed tools; psychological questionnaires also resulted in duplicate information and recent findings were restrictive, designating the current practices that were top best possible ways of assessing declines in modifying the Strategy that was quite general.

articleTitle: Digital Twin-Driven Augmented Vision System for Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The real-time augmented vision system for digital dual-based healthcare applications aimed at improving patient monitoring, diagnostic accuracy, and surgical outcomes. By integrating augmented reality (AR) and digital twin technologies, the proposed system uses real-time data from wearable sensors and patient records to create a dynamic virtual model of the patient's health. This virtual model allows healthcare workers to visualize and communicate key health indicators directly in their field of view during a procedure. Initial evaluations in a simulated environment show that the system has the potential to increase surgical accuracy, reduce diagnostic errors, and improve patient outcomes.

articleTitle: AI Powered Crop Recommendation: A Machine Learning Approach to Sustainable Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Agriculture is the main source of income or business for most people, especially in India. In addition, it is the main food source and contributes significantly to global food security. India needs better agricultural products as the world's population rises. Choosing crops for a particular area based on the local soil and environmental conditions is the first step in satisfying the desire for increased yield. Selecting the appropriate crop for the area will increase the farmer's profit and yield while also meeting the increasing need for yields. Consequently, this research study develops a machine learning strategy for crop selection based on soil parameters. For this reason, the machine learning approach is developed in this research work for crop selection based on the soil conditions and climate changes in the specific area, which primarily enhances the profitability and the requirement of increased production. The research objective creates an improved model that optimizes gradient boosting with evolutionary feature selection for the purpose of selecting appropriate crops using a crop recommendation dataset that includes data on the temperature, humidity, rainfall, and other environmental factors specific to the area as well as soil conditions like Nitrogen, Potassium, Phosphorus, and PH level. Because there are some missing attribute values in the dataset, the KNN technique is used to fill in these values. The genetic algorithm is used in this model's implementation to choose the best features that will boost its performance, and the gradient boosting approach is used to estimate the recommended crop for the area. This distinctive approach's performance is compared with existing algorithms, and the suggested model yields the greatest accuracy of 98.5 in that comparison.

articleTitle: VLSI Circuit Architectures for Scalable IoT Implementations
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Designing circuits for IoT devices presents significant challenges, particularly in security and power management. With billions of devices operating globally, ensuring robust security and efficient energy usage is crucial. Physically Unclonable Functions (PUFs) are essential for providing unique, tamper-resistant identities to devices. However, creating compact PUFs that function reliably under varying conditions is challenging. This thesis introduces two innovative PUF designs using ultra-small analog circuits that generate temperature-independent outputs. Key contributions include an ultra-compact, robust PUF based on PTAT voltage generators, reducing area by 8.3 times while doubling robustness, and a To transform a 6T-SRAM (Six-Transistor Static Random Access Memory) array into a robust analog Physical Unclonable Function (PUF) with minimal overhead. Additionally, it addresses energy harvesting (EH) for IoT sensor nodes, where efficient power management is critical. To reduce efficiency losses in Power Management Units (PMUs), a capacitor buffers energy flow, especially in hybrid energy storage systems.

articleTitle: Forecasting Sports Performance Using Historic Data and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Analyzing Olympic performance and forecasting medal results using past data has been transformed by machine learning. The goal of this research is to use Random Forest Regression, a powerful machine learning approach, to forecast which nations will take home Olympic medals. The model is intended to precisely predict results for future Olympic events by combining a number of characteristics, including gender, event type, country (NOC), and historical medal data. To ensure thorough analysis, the project classifies and processes data from various inputs using sophisticated feature engineering approaches. An easy-to-use internet interface is used to generate real-time forecasts, making them accessible and user-friendly. These predictions help with strategic planning and performance improvement by offering insightful information about a nation's possible medal hopes. This method shows the strong synergy between data science and sports analytics by merging machine learning with historical research to forecast Olympic performance in an effective, scalable, and creative way.

articleTitle: Wild Animal Species Detection System using Embedded Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Detecting wild animal species using embedded devices requires the use of a variety of technologies to monitor and identify animals in their natural environments. This field typically collects data about wildlife using sensors, cameras, communication modules, and, in some cases, artificial intelligence algorithms. The primary goals of deploying embedded devices for wild animal species detection are conservation and research. Researchers can collect vital data for conservation initiatives, wildlife management, and scientific research by tracking animal numbers, behaviors, and habitats. Embedded devices frequently include sensors such as motion sensors, temperature sensors, and accelerometers to detect the presence of animals and collect environmental data. Camera traps are widely employed for animal monitoring. These are outfitted with motion sensors and cameras that capture photographs or movies of animals as they pass. Many embedded devices have communication modules such as GPS, GSM, and satellite connectivity, allowing researchers to access data and get alarms in real-time. These gadgets are often compact, low-power, and tough, built to survive extreme environmental conditions while using little energy. Monitoring endangered species to determine population trends, habitat use, and threats. Exploring animal behavior, migration patterns, and ecological connections. Identifying places with high wildlife activity to reduce confrontations between humans and wildlife.

articleTitle: Low-Cost IoT Mesh Network for Real-Time Indoor Air Quality Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Indoor air quality (IAQ) has become an increasingly important consideration due to its impact on human health and well-being. Many existing IAQ monitoring systems are expensive, complex, and difficult to scale for widespread deployment, especially in residential and small commercial settings. This paper presents a low-cost and scalable Internet of Things (IoT)-based solution for real-time IAQ monitoring using the ESP32-S3 microcontroller, MQ-135 gas sensor, and DHT11 temperature and humidity sensor. The system utilizes Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) for communication, enabling wireless transmission of data to mobile devices from IoT nodes. The network uses the ESP-NOW protocol to create a robust mesh network that enables efficient data transmission across large indoor spaces. The design prioritizes low power consumption, ease of deployment, and cost-effectiveness, making it suitable for smart home and small-scale commercial applications. The proposed solution aims to address the limitations of traditional IAQ monitoring systems, which are often expensive, difficult to scale, and lack real-time, easily accessible data. The system measures key IAQ parameters, including CO2, temperature, and humidity, providing real-time data accessible through a mobile app. The calibration of the designed IoT nodes accomplished through industry standard “Extech SD800: CO2, Humidity and Temperature Datalogger”, Experimental results demonstrate the system's accuracy, reliability, and low power consumption, making it a promising solution for continuous IAQ monitoring.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Linear Integrated Array Antenna for ITU Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Theresearch work is to design a new linearly integrated array antenna which is optimized in millimetre waves for high transmission of radiation signals. The proposed design is compared with the standard application of ITU rectangular antennas. Simulations are depicted, indicating that the FR4 substrate prototype linear integrated array antenna has superior radiation intensity over the rectangular antenna at 2.4 GHz, 0.6263 dB and at 6 GHz at 0.723 dB. Frequency-wise, it covers up to 5.9 GHz and is very superior in performance on microwave frequency around 5.6 GHz at return loss with a value of -43.4834 dB. With a 5.0 dB higher performance compared with the rectangular antennas (2.9 dB), it shows better directivity. Moreover, the geometry has a substantial gain of 2.8 dB for 5G and V2X applications, which surpasses the standard antenna gain of 1.8dB. Conclusion Results The final results show the applicability of this new type of antenna for high-performance wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: An Overview of UPFC Applications in Stability Analysis of Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Maintenance and reliability are the main concerns in modern power systems. With the advancements in transmission system infrastructure development and the rise in transmission voltage, it is necessary to enhance the system's power transfer capability and controllability. This can be achieved with the aid of power electronics-based devices called FACTS. This work presents an overview of opportunities for stability analysis of power systems using UPFC. The UPFC is a versatile FACTS (Flexible AC Transmission System) device that can regulate both actual and reactive power flow in transmission lines, providing greater flexibility in power system management. This review study illustrates that the integration of UPFC significantly improves system performance under normal and abnormal conditions. Also, the implementation challenges are discussed.

articleTitle: Cloud-Based AIOT Soil Monitoring System for Earthworms
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Determining the soil conditions that are favourable to earthworm species is vital for maintaining soil health and improving agricultural yield. Timely reactions are constrained by the work-intensive nature of conventional soil monitoring techniques and their lack of real-time insights into characteristics of the soil. In order to address these issues, we created an Internet of Things (IoT) cloud-based soil monitoring system that tracks pH and moisture levels, two factors that are essential for earthworm survival, while utilizing clustering algorithms for categorizing soil conditions and Random Forest machine learning algorithms for predicting optimal habitats. This state-of-the-device enables more informed soil management decisions by offering cloud-based trend analysis visuals and fast feedback via an LCD display. The method effectively improves the detection of suitable circumstances for earthworm habitats by combining innovative sensor technology with real-time data transmission and processing. Compared to conventional techniques, our system reveals significant gains in graphical representation and data collection as well as automated choices. Collectively, these features promote a more proactive approach to soil management, improving the fertility of the soil and creating optimal conditions for earthworms. With potential uses across various precision farming domains, our methodology provides a significant instrument for sustainable agriculture.

articleTitle: Development of Medical Image Retrieval and Classification using YOLOv7 Segmentation and Inception V3 Classifier
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This research study proposes a novel image retrieval and classification system that aims to overcome the limitations of conventional image retrieval systems. The system is designed for the purpose of conducting searches. The process of image retrieval and classification consists of two distinct stages: training and testing. During the training phase, images are acquired from a publicly accessible data source and then processed through the segmentation stage. During the segmentation process, images are partitioned using the YOLOv7 model. The segmented images are subsequently sent into the Inception V3 Net for classification. The database contains the classified images as well. During the testing phase, images of user-related queries are taken to accurately retrieve corresponding images from the database. In this scenario, the deep features of the query images are obtained using the Inception V3 Net. The extracted features are compared to the stored trained image features in the database using the Euclidean distance similarity function. In order to assess the efficacy of the model, the empirical results are compared to previous image retrieval algorithms using several simulated metrics.

articleTitle: A Hybrid CNN-GRU Approach for Enhanced LOS/NLOS Signal Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Wireless communication relies heavily on Line-of- Sight (LoS) and Non-Line-of-Sight (NLoS) classification, especially in situations with many barriers where precise prediction is difficult. To improve the classification of LoS and NLoS scenarios, we present a model in this study that combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs). Using their capacity to recognize complex patterns and localized correlations in high-dimensional multipath signal profiles, CNNs are used to extract spatial characteristics from signal data. By capturing temporal dependencies, GRUs make it possible to analyze sequential signal fluctuations more thoroughly. The first step in the suggested method is gathering signal data and generating multipath and delay-speed profiles. The accuracy of LoS/NLoS classification is then greatly increased by applying CNNs and GRUs to the data. This approach improves wireless communication performance under difficult circumstances by providing a reliable solution for settings with significant impediments.

articleTitle: Enhancing Tourism Experiences Through Immersive Technologies: The Role of Virtual and Augmented Reality
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This study examines the influence of immersive technologies, particularly Virtual Reality (VR) and Augmented Reality (AR), on the tourism industry, emphasizing recent developments and the obstacles encountered in their integration. VR and AR deliver transforming experiences through virtual tours, interactive guides, and augmented on-site information, so redefining the marketing, exploration, and enjoyment of destinations. Current systems encounter obstacles like elevated development expenses, technical intricacies in attaining realistic and engaging user experiences, and constraints in accessibility and scalability across many platforms. This study emphasizes cutting-edge technologies such Unity3D, Vuforia, and Blender 3D, elucidating their functions in the creation of a VR and AR application aimed at enhancing tourism experiences. A framework is designed to address these problems, delivering scalable, user-friendly, and visually immersive applications that may establish new benchmarks for accessibility and environmental sustainability in tourism. The findings illustrate the potential of VR and AR to enhance travel experiences by making them more engaging, accessible, and sustainable, highlighting the necessity for continuous study and innovation to fully realize their capabilities within the tourism sector.

articleTitle: Compact Convolutional Transformers for Multiple Predominant Instrument Recognition in Polyphonic Music
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: In this study, we address the challenge of identifying multiple predominant instruments in polyphonic music using Compact Convolution Transformers (CCT). With the emergence of Transformers in language processing and their subsequent applications in computer vision, there has been a trend towards larger models requiring extensive training data. However, these models prove inefficient with limited training data and are challenging to scale for large image sizes. Swin Transformer (SwinT) attempts to alleviate these concerns with its shifted window approach but still demands substantial training data. In contrast, CCT offer advantages such as operating effectively with smaller datasets, requiring fewer training parameters, and facilitating efficient feature extraction through convolution blocks. We compared the proposed method with Vision Transformers (ViT) and SwinT, demonstrating improvements in parameter efficiency, image size, and training speed. Additionally, we evaluated the performance of our approach against the state-of-the-art Han model. Han's approach utilizes sliding window analysis and aggregation strategies, significantly improving instrument recognition. Our findings indicate that CCTs can replace existing state-of-the-art networks for identifying predominant instruments in polyphonic music, eliminating the need for aggregation strategies or sliding window approaches.

articleTitle: AI-Enhanced Cognitive Therapy: Personalized Guidance via Adaptive Agents with Voice Analysis and Stress Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This research presents a novel framework for AI-Enhanced Automated Cognitive Therapy (AECT) that integrates cutting-edge technologies to provide personalized and effective mental health support. AECT leverages refined Transformer-based conversational agents,advanced voice analysis,and physiological signal processing to offer a comprehensive therapeutic experience. The proposed system incorporates deep learning models for voice analysis and facial emotion recognition,achieving high accuracy in identifying emotional subtleties and stress levels. By combining these advanced technologies,AECT provides a personalized and engaging therapeutic experience,demonstrating the potential to significantly impact mental well-being and improve therapeutic outcomes worldwide.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Examination of Deep Learning Based Tea Leaf Disease Identification Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This research provides a comprehensive review of state-of-the-art deep learning (DL)-based approaches for disease detection and diagnosis in tea plants. The study reviews various DL methods, particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), focusing on their implementations, datasets used, and performance metrics. While existing studies have shown promising results, the review highlights the challenges and limitations of current approaches. By identifying these challenges and proposing future research directions, this study aims to guide further research in this area and contribute to the development of more robust and effective DL-based solutions for disease detection and management in tea plants.

articleTitle: IoMT-Based Parkinson Therapeutic System
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The proposed work is a therapeutic system based on the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) designed for an accurate and efficient management of Parkinson's disease. The system is proposed to use advanced techniques of data collection and extraction of features for improving diagnostic accuracy and monitoring of patients. The proposed framework merges IoMT with AI to implement real-time analysis application, thus working towards reducing the burden on healthcare providers while empowering the patients to exercise better control over their symptoms.

articleTitle: Voice Chat - Bringing Chats to Life Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
