articleTitle: Augmented Reality Navigation Assistance for PLM Offices Integrating Chatbot Functionality for Appointment Scheduling and Information Access
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Navigating large university campuses can be challenging, especially for new students and visitors unfamiliar with the area. To address this, an Augmented Reality (AR) mobile application is proposed to improve navigation and information access within Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila. This app combines AR-based navigation and Points of Interest (POIs) with a chatbot, offering users real-time spatial guidance and answers to frequently asked questions about campus facilities and services. Evaluation was conducted using the ISO 25010 software quality framework, assessing Functional Suitability, Reliability, Interaction Capability, and Performance Efficiency. With feedback from 70 participants, the system achieved high satisfaction ratings across all criteria, validating its effectiveness as a campus navigation tool. These findings demonstrate the potential of AR and chatbot integration to improve accessibility and enhance user experience in educational environments.

articleTitle: Temporal Fusion Transformer Based Temporal Convolutional Network Model for Sleep Apnea Detection Using Single-Lead ECG Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Sleep apnea (SA) is a sleep disorder which is characterized by intermittent interruptions in breathing and airflow throughout a sleep cycle. Traditional techniques such as polysomnography (PSG), remain costly, labor-intensive, and require overnight monitoring in specialized labs, which limits its accessibility and scalability. For continuous sleep apnea diagnosis, deep learning models offer a scalable, non-invasive, and economical alternative to multi-sensor PSG monitoring which paves the way for integration into wearable IoT devices for real-time health monitoring. To address the limitations posed by traditional multi-sensor techniques, a novel framework based on Deep Learning techniques is proposed: Temporal Fusion Transformer-based Temporal Convolutional Network (TFT-TCN), designed for the detection of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) with the use of single-lead ECG signals. The TCN module uses dilated convolutions to extract temporal features efficiently whereas the TFT module employs Gated Residual Network (GRN), Adaptive Fusion and Multi-Head Attention to compute attention scores and fuse the feature vectors. Overall, the proposed TCN-TFT model achieved a noteworthy Accuracy of 89.55 %, FI-Score of 89.3% and AUC score of 0.95.

articleTitle: A Survey on Breast Cancer Prediction using Various Deep Learning and Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Breast Cancer continues to be a predominant contributor to mortality associated with cancer among women on a global scale. To improve survival rates and treatment consequences, it's necessary to detect issues early and create an accurate diagnosis. In recent years, Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) techniques have shown great promise in medical diagnostics, offering the potential to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of breast cancer detection and prognosis. This research work provides breast cancer prediction using deep learning and machine learning studies on mammograms, ultrasounds, magnetic resonance imaging, and digital pathology images conducted over the past decade. An evaluation of studies from the past ten years highlights how important deep learning and machine learning have been in better patient outcomes and enlarges the accuracy of breast cancer detection. The automation of medical image assessment, machine learning, and deep learning technologies facilitate radiologists and pathologists in rendering more knowledgeable and accurate decisions. This reduction in the probability of human errors culminates in superior diagnostic accuracy and treatment methodologies, thereby ultimately improving the quality of patient care.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Models for Interference Suppression with a Focus on Hybrid Architectures
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Interference in wireless communication systems is a significant challenge towards the attainment of maximum throughput and minimum latency, especially in dynamic and high-noise environments. This research study presents a smart and scalable hybrid Convolutional Autoencoder (CAE) for interference reduction in wireless communication systems with additional Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU). The proposed model uses CAE for effective spatial feature extraction and GRU for capturing temporal dependencies in dynamic interference scenarios. Lightweight architectural enhancements, such as depth wise separable convolutions and reduced parameters of the GRU, balance the computational efficiency and batch-level parallelism for better performance. Therefore, the architecture shows better performance in terms of throughput along with reduced latency compared to traditional DL methods and other variants of hybrid models, making it practical for real-time and limited-resources operation environments. Finally, the challenges and future research directions for advancing DL applications in interference management are outlined.

articleTitle: Energy Conservation Using Piezo Electric Effect Through Modern Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This paper seeks to establish the energy conservation by using piezo-electric effect through some Modern Technology's and the project aims to investigate the application of modern technology in various fields to reduce energy consumption and increase energy efficiency. We focus on three key areas: buildings, transportation, and industry. In each of these areas, we identify the most significant energy consumption sources and potential opportunities for energy savings using modern technology. This aims to explore innovative solutions for sustainable energy generation by harnessing mechanical energy from human movement. This research focuses on integrating piezoelectric cells into everyday footwear and flooring tiles to convert mechanical stress into electrical energy. The project involves designing and fabricating prototypes of energy-harvesting shoes and tiles. The efficiency of energy conversion, the durability of the materials, and the overall feasibility of integrating such systems into daily life will be evaluated. The study will also address the scalability of this technology and its potential impact on reducing the reliance on traditional power sources.

articleTitle: Review on Adaptive Filtering Techniques in Cooperative Localization and Zone-based ECU Architectures for Automotive Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This paper offers a state-of-the-art analysis of the most recent developments in cooperative location estimation using adaptive filters under adverse conditions including compass loss and non-Gaussian noise environment of vehicular networks. Cooperative localization is now an essential feature for autonomous and connected cars and requires reliable algorithms that can handle tricky sensor failures and noise interference. The study is dedicated to the examination of “A Novel Adaptive Filtering for Cooperative Localization Under Compass Failure and Non-Gaussian Noise,” which describes an adaptive filtering approach aimed at reducing localization errors in systems that do not have compass data and when non-Gaussian noise appears. This approach involves the use of adaptive techniques for the accommodation of varying noise levels to improve the order, and accuracy of location characteristics in real-time. Thus, a comparative analysis of the performance and computational complexity of particle filters, Kalman filters, and extended Kalman filters is given based on the analysis of the performance of different adaptive filtering techniques. Further, we discuss the applications and consequences of the proposed filtering framework for autonomous vehicles' localization systems. These results suggest that the proposed adaptive filtering greatly enhances localization performance in the presence of off-nominal sensors to support more reliable car operations in actual environments. In the final section of the paper, some ideas for the further development of robust localization technologies and the application of advanced machine learning to improve the filtering approach and its adaptability are presented.

articleTitle: Identification of Diabetic Retinopathy by Transfer Learning Based Retinal Images
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The human eye is frequently considered to deliver a space into a person's strength because it is only with diabetic retinopathy (DR), a devastating eye illness caused by diabetes mellitus, that one may understand the subject's unprotected surface without invasive operations. There are certain disorders, notably vascular illness, that authority telltale indicators in the eye retina. Microaneurysms (MAs) are primary indicators of diabetic retinopathy (DR), making their detection crucial for an effective screening program that adheres to clinical procedures. Retinal examinations can reveal pathological deviations caused by limited ocular diseases such as arteriosclerosis, diabetes, cardiovascular disease hypertension and stroke. The proposed work introduces image processing algorithms, such as shady object identification, to predict the disorder or improve the contribution frame, thereby improving the perceptibility of vessels in color fundus frames. Following this enhancement, an automated classification algorithm, specifically a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), is executed. The CNN architecture is designed to efficiently extract features from retinal frames, capturing complex patterns connected with diabetic retinopathy. The trained CNN is then assessed on a separate test condition, with its performance system of measurement-accuracy, specificity, recall, and Fl measure-being reported.

articleTitle: Advanced Day-Ahead Photovoltaic Power Prediction through RNN Modeling: Enhancing Forecast Accuracy for Improved Grid Stability
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The day-ahead photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is very important in the management and integration of the PV systems into today's complex power systems especially given the increasing trend in the adoption of the renewable energy-based power systems. The efficiency of PV power output forecast not only improves the stability of the power grid, but also plays a significant role in energy scheduling and the pursuit of the net-zero emission goal. There are certain issues which vary from time to time in the case of solar energy and hence there are certain drawbacks attached with it, for instance predicting of power forecast is one of the major drawback of solar energy production. It has been found that existing approaches are problematic because they are either less accurate or not very adaptive, and also because they are complex to compute, and consequently less reliable, which impacts the potential of energy systems to operate efficiently. In response to these challenges, we introduce an RNN-based model for day-ahead PV power prediction in this paper. By OLS, the proposed model builds on the successful implementation of RNNs in modeling temporal characteristics and nonlinear trends of historical power data to improve the accuracy of the forecast. The RNN model is also capable of learning from other influencing factors since the dataset adopted in this paper embraces diverse and intricate parameters in the analysis of the solar irradiance and other environmental conditions. The results shown here indicate returns that clearly places the RNN-based model ahead of traditional approaches to forecasting as well as DL structures besides the four-fold validation of performances with high scores in MAE, MSE, and MAPE.

articleTitle: Anomaly Detection in Network Traffic Using LSTM with Attention Mechanism and Willow Catkin Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: A new anomaly detection method is presented in this study with the aim of improving the safety and reliability of IoT networks. The attention mechanism and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks are tuned using the new heuristic method known as Willow Catkin Optimization (WCO). LSTM networks excel in capturing the intricate temporal relationships seen in IoT traffic data, and the attention mechanism hones down on the most important aspects, enhancing the model's anomaly detection capabilities. Utilizing WCO, the hyperparameters of the LSTM network are fine-tuned to guarantee peak performance, significantly improving detection accuracy. Internet of Things (IoT) traffic is complex and ever-changing, which the suggested solution takes into account. Using a combination of feature prioritization and temporal pattern recognition, this method efficiently and reliably identifies possible security concerns in IoT contexts. Improving anomaly detection while minimizing false positives, the attention-enhanced LSTM model improved with WCO is particularly suitable for real-world IoT network security. More precise threat detection and improved network resilience are two ways this initiative improves upon previous efforts in the area of Internet of Things cybersecurity.

articleTitle: Automated Glaucoma Detection from Retinal Fundus Images: Leveraging EfficientNetV2 for Enhanced Diagnostic Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Globally, glaucoma is the main cause of permanent blindness; effective treatment depends on early identification. This paper presents an automated glaucoma identification utilizing retinal fundus images using the EfficientNetV2 model, which is well-known for its efficiency and good performance in image classification applications. Using fundus images split into two classes-glaucoma present (1) and glaucoma not present (0) — we used the SMDG-19 dataset. We used oversampling, weighted loss functions, and data augmentation to improve model training and performance and therefore solve the class imbalance present in medical datasets. EfficientNetV2's architecture enables the identification of subtle variations in retinal structures, including the optic nerve head and retinal nerve fiber layer, which are crucial for accurate glaucoma diagnosis. The model achieved an impressive overall accuracy of 93%, with a precision of 0.93 and a recall of 0.96 for glaucoma detection, indicating a high sensitivity in identifying true positive cases. With an F1-score of 0.95, the model likewise clearly balanced recall with accuracy. These results indicate how effectively the EfficientNetV2 model detects glaucoma and suggest its potential utility as a clinical tool for early diagnosis, hence improving patient outcomes. This paper highlights the significant contribution that deep learning techniques provide to enhance diagnosis and medical picture analysis.

articleTitle: Enhanced Network Security: Real-Time Malicious Traffic Detection in SD-WAN Using LSTM-GRU Hybrid Model
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: In today's digital world, network administration has been revolutionized by Software-Defined Wide Area Network (SD-WAN) technology, which offers enhanced management, flexibility, and efficiency across distributed network topologies. This transition also increases susceptibility to security risks, including harmful traffic that could compromise network integrity. This paper proposes a method for real-time malicious traffic detection in SD-WAN networks employing a hybrid deep learning model that incorporates Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) networks. The LSTM-GRU architecture is designed to retrieve both short- and long-term connections in network traffic data, hence improving the model's capacity to reliably identify unusual behavior that signifies security vulnerabilities. The model achieves an impressive detection accuracy of 98.83 %, which proves that it is effective at safeguarding SD-WAN environments. This suggested framework enhances SD-WAN network security by offering a dependable, real-time threat detection system that can be smoothly integrated into current network management protocols to reduce risks and maintain operational continuity.

articleTitle: Insights into Facial Emotion Recognition-A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Facial expression recognition technology is an essential part of the security ecosystem. Facial expression-based emotion recognition is a captivating study area applied in various fields such as human-machine interactions, safety, and health. This method was employed to enhance the accuracy of predicting emotions by identifying, encoding, and extracting relevant information. Deep learning (DL) has been remarkably successful, and its various architectures are now being used to improve performance. This paper's goal is to conduct a study of recent efforts to recognize face emotions using ML, transfer learning, DL, and hybrid methods. Additionally, a classification of current facial emotion analysis techniques is briefly presented. The study also lists and summarizes the approaches' benefits and drawbacks. Challenges like high computational requirements and the limitation of frequency-domain analysis have to emphasize the need for methods that balance accuracy with efficiency. The review also highlights the potential uses of face expression recognition in fields like security, psychology, health care, and human-computer interaction. The review's overall goal is to give a thorough assessment of the current papers on facial expression identification and to suggest areas for further investigation. Finally, we suggest future opportunities for addressing research challenges, including the development of models that capture both spatial and frequency- domain features efficiently, potentially enhancing the reliability and overall performance of FER systems.

articleTitle: Advanced Toxicity Assessment: A BiLSTM Approach for Nanoparticle Safety
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Nanotoxicity prediction is crucial for safeguarding human health and the environment due to the unique properties of nanoparticles (NPs) that lead to unforeseen biological interactions. With growing applications of nanomaterials in consumer products, pharmaceuticals, and industry, early detection of their toxic effects is vital for risk assessment, regulatory compliance, and the informed design of safer materials. In this study, a deep learning (DL) model, Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM), is proposed for the effective prediction of nanoparticle toxicity. Utilizing a publicly available dataset, the model analyzes physicochemical attributes of various NPs, including Al203, Fe203, CuO,Ti02, and ZnO. The dataset encompasses 476 toxic and 405 non-toxic samples, with features such as core size, surface area, and exposure time. The methodology involves rigorous data preprocessing, including outlier detection using Z-scores and one-hot encoding for categorical variables. The BiLSTM architecture processes data in both forward and backward directions, effectively capturing temporal dependencies and enhancing toxicity prediction accuracy. The model's performance was evaluated, achieving remarkable 98.28% accuracy, 98.01 % precision, 97.82% recall, and 97.91 % Fl-score. Additionally, the ROC curve demonstrated excellent discrimination between classes, with an AUC of 0.96. The findings highlight the potential of DL in advancing nanotoxicity prediction, thereby contributing to safer applications of nanotechnology.

articleTitle: Comparative Performance Analysis of SQL and NoSQL Databases for Optimizing Retail and E-Commerce Operations
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic, the rapid growth of online retail, or electronic commerce, has transformed the way consumers fulfil their needs and desires. This expansion introduced new business opportunities that expedites international market growth. The digitalization of economy and consumer behaviour necessitates advancements in technologies and the selection of a database to process incoming customer data. The exponential increase in data has also increased the demand for robust and scalable database management systems. This paper aims to select the most suitable data model for online retail industries by conducting comparative analysis between relational, graph, wide-column, key-value, and document database models. The study explores the performance, strengths, and weaknesses of each model in handling various aspects of retail and e-commerce functionalities, including order processing and customer relationship management (CRM). Each database model is rigorously tested against thousands of records to accurately assess their effectiveness and performance within the retail industry. After deliberate testing, it is discovered that relational databases outshine the other NoSQL databases in terms of client performance - CPU speed in GHz, the CPU utilization and memory usage in percentage, and its capacity in handling large datasets in the e-commerce industry.

articleTitle: Advancing Conversational Chatbots: Optimizing User Interaction and Information Access
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The use of chatbots has expanded significantly in recent years, impacting various fields such as marketing, support systems, education, healthcare, cultural heritage, and entertainment. This presentation explores the growing global interest in chatbots and the factors driving their adoption across these diverse sectors. We examine how societal stereotypes shape chatbot design and discuss the core technologies that underpin these systems. Additionally, we categorize chatbots based on their specialized functions and the needs they meet, and we outline the principles behind modern chatbot design along with key development platforms. The advancement of Natural Language Processing (NLP) has been crucial in enhancing chatbot capabilities, enabling more natural and human-like interactions. Voice-activated chatbots like Siri and Alexa showcase how NLP can improve user engagement through conversational interfaces. Recent progress in machine learning has further boosted the accuracy and effectiveness of NLP, making chatbots a valuable tool for various applications. Our discussion highlights the exciting prospects of NLP-powered chatbots in personalized learning and advocates for continued research to unlock their full potential. We also review rule-based training approaches, such as using Artificial Intelligence Markup Language (AIML), which enable chatbots to operate based on predefined response patterns.

articleTitle: Optimizing Trust-Based Routing with a Hybrid TCN-ANN Model for IoT RPL Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: IoT networks are increasingly vulnerable to security threats, especially from malicious nodes that can interfere with network performance and stability. The Routing Protocol for Low Power and Lossy Networks (RPL) is a standardized protocol created for Internet of Things (IoT) networks, designed to enable efficient and reliable routing in resource-constrained environment. However, it is susceptible to attacks like blackhole, flooding, and Destination Oriented Directed Acyclic Graph (DODAG) inconsistency, which can undermine network integrity and performance. The study focuses on strengthening IoT network security by integrating deep learning techniques with trust-based routing protocols. Using the ROUT-4-2023 dataset, the objective was to develop a robust intrusion detection system capable of identifying and mitigating malicious activities. The methodology employed includes a systematic preprocessing phase followed by feature extraction and classification. Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) was used for extracting time-series features and the classification was done using Artificial Neural Network (ANN) which achieved an accuracy of 97%. Additionally, a trust-based routing mechanism was incorporated, assigning trust scores to nodes based on the classification results. This approach ensured secure and efficient routing bypassing malicious nodes. The model's performance was evaluated using various metrics, demonstrating high classification accuracy and reliable intrusion detection.

articleTitle: Enhancing Road Safety: Analyzing Driver Behavior Through AI-Driven Monitoring Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This study aims to address the significant threat of safe driving in terms of the characteristics of drivers, including anger, attention, fatigue, and drowsiness. In an increasingly intelligent society, monitoring drivers effectively and determining unusual behavior is very important for the prevention of car accidents. Despite the current emphasis on various means of assessing driver behavior, much remains to be understood about the interplay between driver health, vehicle conditions, and unusual driving habits. The work will be presenting a comprehensive classification of behavior detection methods, evaluating their effectiveness, and indicating critical open issues in the field. The study involves modeling of driving behavior and anomaly detection using AI -enhanced image processing, signal processing techniques, and traditional algorithm-based methods. Contemporary methods have been classified into mathematics, machine learning, and deep learning techniques, and there is a comprehensive review of the state-of-the-art. The talk focuses on important findings and issues and promotes further research to establish innovative approaches that enhance highway safety through better surveillance systems.

articleTitle: Advanced Strategies for Detecting Ransomware Threats
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Ransomware is one of the key threats that have been created to lock the important services and data. New techniques like machine learning and blockchain are being used for enhancing the detection and mitigation process. However, these continue to face major challenges in terms of time lags arising out of delayed technology adoptions, gaps in security protocols, and inaccessibility of certain detection mechanisms within the systems to identify real-time advanced ransomware. In addition, fast restoration and ensuring minimum downtime for operations is still difficult. tackling these challenges by the integration of Machine Learning with traditional security techniques to enable early threat detection, accurate mitigation strategies, and quick restoration. Besides, it employs machine learning toward the correct identification of ransomware behavior and continuous adaptation to developing threats. The goal is to develop a hard, anticipatory defensive system that incurs the least possible blow from ransomware, thereby focusing on future research directions to better perfect such technologies.

articleTitle: Enabling Protection for Critical Infrastructure through Security and Privacy in the Industrial Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Industrial Internet of Things can improve critical infrastructure in energy, transportation, and manufacturing. However, IIoT device and system integration opened security weaknesses that bad actors may exploit, causing huge disruptions and financial losses. IoT network security and privacy must be prioritized to protect key infrastructure. IIoT security issues and solutions are examined in this research. First, we take a look at the state of security and the unique risks that industrial IoT devices are up against, including hacking, illegal access, and cyber-physical assaults. Then, to lessen the impact of these dangers, we investigate cutting-edge security solutions, such as authentication, encryption, and access control systems. Building a robust security architecture specifically for IIoT applications is one of the main goals of the project. To improve safety and anonymity, this system uses cutting-edge innovation like blockchain, AI, and edge computing. We also talk about how privacy-preserving methods like differential privacy and anonymization are important for keeping sensitive information safe while allowing data sharing for analysis and operations. We assess the efficacy of the suggested security protocols and procedures using a battery of case studies and simulations. Reducing the attack surface and improving the resilience of IIoT systems can be achieved by a multi-layered security approach that includes effective privacy protections. We conclude by outlining our research's larger implications, which include the importance of standardization, regulatory compliance, and stakeholder collaboration in ensuring the safe and privacy-protecting deployment of IIoT technologies in vital infrastructure. Protecting vital infrastructure from cyber threats is our ultimate goal, and our work helps build IIoT systems that are more secure and dependable.

articleTitle: ValueTrix: A Mobile Application for Inventory Management with Optical Character Recognition (OCR) Integration and Profitability Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: ValueTrix is a mobile app created for A2 Pharmacy in the pharmaceutical industry by using modern technologies like Optical Character Recognition (OCR), Natural Language Processing (NLP), and Predictive Analytics. It helps businesses by improving stock management, automating daily processes, and providing accurate financial forecasts. Using ARIMA, it predicts profitability based on sales and inventory data. The integration of OCR technology, which results in 98% accuracy rate higher than the 95% reported in similar studies by Shahin et al. [1]. Additionally, the app's NLP-NER algorithm simplifies the organization of purchase orders and sales data, ensuring everything is accurately sorted for smoother operations. Unlike expensive machinery, this mobile solution provides an effective and affordable alternative for businesses. By addressing problems like manual inventory management errors and inefficiencies, ValueTrix empowers better decision-making and operational efficiency. Success satisfaction is rated highly at 4.74 % per ISO 25010:2023. ValueTrix demonstrates that mobile-based emerging technologies can drive business growth, promote sustainability, and enhance profitability management by enabling firms to adjust stock levels, control expenses, and plan for demand fluctuations effectively.

articleTitle: Optimized Energy Efficient Routing Network using Lévy Flight with Seagull Optimization in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) is comprised of infinite Sensor Nodes (SNs), which are low-priced, low-power, and minute features. These nodes are data-centric and have the responsibility to gather important data in the pretentious area and transfer the data to the sink node (control base or center station) in a single- or multi-hop technique. To commence WSNs to sustain in a healthy and secure atmosphere, safety devices according to identity authentication and cryptography have been proposed to oppose outside threats on WSNs. Routing is predominant in WSNs for optimizing their efficiency, scalability, and longevity. Routing represents a process of describing the optimum routes for the data transmission from SNs to the sink. Dynamic routing guarantees reliable and timely data transmission however balances the network load and decreases energy intake. WSNs can gain improved routing using metaheuristics that outcomes in lengthy operational lifespans and better performance of the network. This study presents an Optimized Energy Efficient Routing Network using Lévy Flight with Seagull Optimization Algorithm (OEERN-LFSOA) technique in WSN. The presented OEERN-LFSOA technique mainly focusing on enhancing the energy efficiency and lifespan of WSNs using routing approaches. To achieve this, the presented OEERN-LFSOA method involves the integration of the Lévy Flight with Seagull Optimization Algorithm (LFSOA) model. Furthermore, the presented OEERN-LFSOA method obtains a fitness function for exploiting the lifetime and diminishing consumption of energy. A comprehensive set of simulations was directed to show the performance of the OEERN-LFSOA method. The experimental outcomes stated that the OEERN-LFSOA method achieves better performance than other recent techniques.

articleTitle: 5G Deployment Challenges and Solutions: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The connection of a massive number of devices can offer unprecedented speed, and low latency across industries promised by the deployment of 5G. The official launch of 5G networks offers a unique set of challenges that differentiate it from earlier generations. The 5G introduces a few key challenges such as spectrum scarcity, the need for extensive infrastructure upgrades, cybersecurity concerns, and high energy demands. Additionally, there are logistical and regulatory challenges hence there is a requirement for the deployment of a dense network of small cells because of uses of higher frequencies in 5G. This work reviews the primary challenges confronted in the deployment of 5G. Enabling advancements in IoT, self-directed vehicles, smart cities, and other emerging applications are unlocking the full budding of 5G by addressing these obstacles is essential. Also, this paper explores innovative solutions, including spectrum sharing, energy-efficient network designs, and advanced antenna technologies. These challenges are very helpful to researchers to design and create more innovative implementations of 5G that leads a new era.

articleTitle: Categorization of Colorectal Polyps using Convolutional Neural Networks for Enhanced Diagnostic Accuracy and Early Detection in Colorectal Cancer Screening
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Colon cancer is a serious health risk that increases human disease and death. Histological analysis is necessary for a definitive diagnosis of this illness. A promising approach to the study of colon cancer is the integration of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in digital image processing, especially with whole-slide imaging. Accurately classifying colon adenocarcinomas is essential for efficient testing. Creating a system that uses image analysis to recognize and classify colon adenocarcinomas by utilizing certain preparatory techniques to develop a unique computer program that use a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to enhance and analyze digital pathology images. By using machine intelligence to automate the diagnosis of cancer, more people can be evaluated more quickly and affordably, improving the effectiveness and accessibility of healthcare evaluations. This automation is made possible by the use of state-of-the-art methods for complex digital image manipulation and advanced pattern identification in data. The findings show that the suggested framework has an astounding accuracy rate of up to 99% when it comes to the careful analysis of cancer tissues. By enhancing the model's generalization over bigger datasets and evaluating its resilience in diverse clinical settings, we hope to advance this research. By using this technique, medical professionals will be able to develop a trustworthy automated system for identifying various forms of colon cancer.

articleTitle: Hair Style Recommendations using CNN and AR
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This research begins with the collecting of a varied dataset of annotated facial photos to ensure accurate representation across populations. The photographs will be pre-processed to standardize their size, illumination, and orientation. On this dataset, we will fine-tune a pre-trained CNN, such as ResNet50, to identify various face forms before evaluating accuracy against a separate test set. Furthermore, we will create a dataset of facial photos combined with various haircuts classified by face shape, and use the CNN to extract relevant features and embeddings. A matching algorithm will match user facial features to hairdo embeddings, ranking recommendations according to similarity metrics. The AR component will leverage ARKit or ARCore for real-time face tracking, allowing users to realistically test on different haircuts overlayed on their live camera feeds. The final solution will be available on mobile and online platforms, with a user-friendly design and options for saving preferred haircuts and providing feedback. This project tackles the demand for a more engaging and individualized hairstyle picking experience, utilizing advanced AI and AR technologies to improve customer happiness and interactivity.

articleTitle: Bitcoin Price Prognosis Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This research explores the application of machine learning techniques to predict Bitcoin price dynamics. Bitcoin, as a decentralized digital currency, has garnered significant attention due to its high volatility and potential for rapid value fluctuations. This study aims to develop a machine learning model that analyzes historical Bitcoin price data to identify patterns and predict future price trends. While precise short-term predictions may be challenging, the model can provide valuable insights into overall price trends and inform investment strategies. This research contributes to a better understanding of Bitcoin price dynamics and has the potential to assist investors in making more informed decisions.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Database Models for Data Management and Security: Evaluating MySQL, Azure Cosmos DB, ScyllaDB, Couchbase, and Firestore in a Student Record System
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This research study explores the strengths and weaknesses of different database management system models focusing on data creation, manipulation, retrieval, as well as access control and data integrity. Here, five database systems are compared: MySQL, Microsoft Azure Cosmos DB, ScyllaDB, Couchbase, and Firestore Firebase. Key findings show that relational models such as MySQL are suitable for structured data and are designed for handling detailed queries, whereas non-relational models such as Microsoft Azure Cosmos DB and Firestore are highly flexible in nature and can be used for unstructured data. Scylla DB and Couchbase both have high performance for specific workloads but face data integrity and transaction support issues. Hence, it is concluded that there cannot be an appropriate data model for all circumstances. Relational models are more suited for complex transactions and structured data, while non-relational models are better for large amounts of unstructured data. Therefore, this study assists database administrators and IT specialists in the selection of an appropriate database management system for the effective management and security of data.

articleTitle: Traffic Sign Categorization Using YOLO Algorithm: Leveraging Real-Time Object Detection for Improved Road Safety
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Traffic signs, and navigation provide drivers with crucial information about speed limits, hazards and are essential for maintaining road safety. Detecting these signs and classifying in real-time plays a vital for autonomous driving systems, as timely information can prevent accidents and ensure compliance with traffic regulations. This paper presents a traffic sign detection system based on the YOLOv8 algorithm, known for its high-speed object detection capabilities, addressing challenges such as occlusion, small object detection, and adverse lighting conditions. The system is trained using a dataset of traffic signs sourced from Roboflow, capturing various types of traffic signs under different environmental conditions, such as lighting, weather, and occlusion scenarios. By using advanced feature extraction techniques, we have visualize the critical features that proposed for the model's classification decisions. The results confirm the efficacy and real-time applications in autonomous vehicles and smart traffic management systems of YOLOv8, indicating the intelligence potential for widespread adoption in the field of vehicles transportation systems.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Intrusion Detection and Prevention Systems in 5G Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: The advent of 5G technology revolutionizes connectivity, offering high-speed data transmission, ultra-reliable low-latency communication, and enhanced capacity for a multitude of devices. However, these advancements introduce complex cybersecurity challenges, as the expanded attack surface makes networks more vulnerable to intrusions and malicious activities. Traditional intrusion detection and prevention systems (IDPS) often fall short in effectively identifying and mitigating sophisticated threats due to their reliance on static algorithms and limited adaptability. To address these limitations, this research proposes an AI-powered IDPS leveraging advanced machine learning models, including Support Vector Machines (SVM), CatBoost, LightGBM, and Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN). The proposed model focuses on real-time data processing and anomaly detection, utilizing a comprehensive dataset featuring critical network traffic attributes such as packet size, protocol type, source and destination IP addresses, duration, and threat level. The integration of these methodologies facilitates improved detection accuracy and adaptability to evolving threats. Results indicate that the TCN model outperforms other methodologies, achieving a superior accuracy of 98.61%. The model's high accuracy highlights its effectiveness in identifying both benign and malicious traffic within 5G networks, demonstrating its potential as a robust solution for modern cybersecurity challenges. By advancing the capabilities of intrusion detection systems in 5G, this research contributes significantly to enhancing network security and establishing a safer digital landscape.

articleTitle: Personalized Learning Platform using Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This research proposes a complete framework for solving the difficulties of poor student management and high attrition rates in Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) through the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies. The framework for mitigating these challenges is presented in this research study. In this study, a multi-pronged strategy is utilized and variety of methods such as discussion forums, content curation, peer to peer content and collaborative projects are investigated. The exploration of AI driven adaptive learning and evaluation methods to enhance the experience of taking massive MOOC is the primary focus of this research. The result findings indicate the efficiency of AI powered adaptive quiz production is giving significance evaluations of student performance. It also represents significance of standardized assessment method and co-effective platforms to integrate the Adaptive Educational Systems. Further, the study indicates essential aspects for improvement within existing MOOC infrastructures. The essential area aspects include personalization driven by AI, elements of gamification and enhanced interactivity. In evaluating the problem-solving skill and delivering personalized feedback, innovative evaluation methos such as Script Concordance evaluations became effective according to comparative review of MOOC platforms. This research also differentiates between general MOOC and connectivity MOOC(c-MOOC) to address the distinct issues in the process of encouraging student engagement. This study presents a unique framework using AI to provide individualized learning experience and incorporates personality test to determine the interest of learners. It also suggests the appropriate career pathways and employs a comprehensive set of evaluation metrics to examine the cognitive capacities and learning development. Through the strategic integration of AI methods such as expanded interactive features and adaptive assessment methods, this study develops multi dimensional method to enhancing the learner's ability to keep data from MOOC and achieve personalized learning outcomes.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study on Combined Economic Emission Dispatch Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Economic Emission Load Dispatch (EELD), the combination of economic efficiency and environmental sustainability in power system operation, has arisen as a critical challenge in the current era of power generation and distribution. This review paper provides an in-depth review of the application of machine learning methods to tackle the inherent complexity of EELD. It encompasses the latest advancements and notable trends in this sector. The review begins by explaining the essential concepts and goals of EELD, highlighting the importance of balancing operating costs and lowering greenhouse gas emissions. EELD solutions have been built on traditional optimization approaches such as Linear Programming and Genetic Algorithms. However, machine learning techniques have recently gained popularity due to their capacity to deal with power systems' complex, non-linear interactions. This paper aims to analyze the strengths and limits of several algorithms in optimizing generation schedules while ensuring that they adhere to emission regulations. Moreover, this paper explores the role of data-driven methodologies in EELD, highlighting the importance of precise data collection and preprocessing. This statement elucidates the incorporation of exogenous variables, such as meteorological predictions and energy consumption trends, into EELD (Energy Efficient Load Dispatch) models, emphasizing their influence on augmenting the efficacy of decision-making procedures.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Early Heart Failure Prediction: A Hybrid Method Using ECG Signal Analysis and the Framingham Risk Score
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: This study introduces a hybrid IoT-based health monitoring system aimed at early prediction of heart disease, which combines real-time ECG data with the Framingham Risk Score (FRS) through machine learning techniques. Conventional models, although efficient, frequently exhibit limitations in their adaptability to real-time data and precision in intricate situations. The proposed hybrid approach mitigates these limitations by integrating the advantages of traditional statistical models with deep learning techniques. An Arduino module acquires real-time ECG signals, which are integrated with patient demographic and clinical data to create robust predictive models. The system utilizes a Random Forest Classifier for the analysis of FRS data and EfficientNetB0 for the classification of ECG signals, thereby delivering precise and comprehensive evaluations of heart health. This integration facilitates ongoing monitoring, prompt detection, and tailored treatment, meeting the demand for accessible and economical solutions in clinical and remote healthcare environments. The hybrid approach improves the system's capacity to detect subtle ECG patterns by integrating established risk factors, thereby connecting traditional methods with advanced machine learning techniques. Preliminary results indicate notable enhance-ments in accuracy: the Random Forest Classifier reached 90.23%, whereas EfficientNetB0 attained 97.11%. These findings under- score the system's potential for early diagnosis, preventive health- care, and informed decision-making, thereby facilitating timely interventions and enhancing patient outcomes.

articleTitle: A Review of Temporally Ordered Routing Algorithm Protocol's Challenges and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: MANETs are characteristically dynamic, as nodes often move, which can create difficulties in ensuring stable and efficient communication routes. The recent work on TORA is QoS improved variant of TORA designed to optimize routing based on use-specific QoS requirement. This review is to discuss improvements that make Temporally Ordered Routing Algorithm to improve its performance in connectivity and reduce the routing delay in dynamic environments. Knowing the problems of starting stage TORA protocol, specifically its weakness to rapid changes in network and delays in route convergence. To solve these problems, we can use adaptive methods for route maintenance, with this a hybrid routing method that uses both proactive and reactive methods. These advancements can make it easier to find the routes rapidly, make stronger connections when nodes are in movement and ultimately improving the overall efficiency of TORA for use in MANETs.

articleTitle: Blockchain Enabled E-Commerce Supply Chain Management
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Blockchain technology has emerged as a transforma-tive innovation in e-commerce supply chain management, offering unprecedented levels of transparency, security, and operational efficiency. By enhancing data integrity, mitigating fraud, and improving traceability, blockchain is reshaping traditional supply chain processes. This paper presents a novel Blockchain-Enabled E-Commerce Supply Chain Management System (BEECSS) designed to address critical challenges, including inefficiencies, data manipulation, and the lack of trust among stakeholders. The system incorporates a tailored blockchain framework that integrates secure, immutable record-keeping with smart contracts to automate and validate essential supply chain activities, such as product creation, ownership transfer, and real-time status updates. BEECSS is built on a robust blockchain architecture that ensures scalability and reliability, deploys smart contracts for process automation and enforcement, and seamlessly integrates with existing e-commerce platforms to enhance interoperability and data flow. The system's effectiveness is demonstrated through performance metrics, including transaction speed, transparency, and error rate, showcasing its potential to significantly improve supply chain transparency, optimize operational efficiency, and foster stakeholder trust. This work establishes a solid foundation for future research and paves the way for the large-scale adoption of blockchain technology in global e-commerce ecosystems.
